Pull request opened by stoccotommaso02: Aggiunto DatabaseConnector. [ARGO-59] La classe DatabaseConnection attua le query definite attualmente, basandosi sulla classe streamlit.connection.SQLConnection e i metodi che fornisce. I particolari legati alla connessione del database sono definiti nel file secrets.toml Il layout dei file, visto anche il refactoring e le altre puill request aperte, è da rivisitare e per questo sono in draft della PR ### Breve descrizione metodi #### Selezione - Metodo fetch user, tramite username - Metodo fetch dictionary, tramite name o id (va specificato tramite argomento della funzione) - Valore ritornato: Una riga di dataframe contentente le informazioni della riga cercata se esistente, vuota altrimenti #### Inserimento dizionario - Valore ritornato: True se l'operazione ha successo, False se si tenta di inserire un nome nullo o una stringa vuota - Errori sollevati: ValueError se si tenta di inserire un dizionario dati con un nome già presente nel database #### Rimozione dizionario dati - Valore ritornato: true se l'operazione ha successo, False se la selezione di quella entry non produce risultato (ossia: il dizionario dati con quella chiave già non esiste) oppure il field specificato non è correto #### Update dizionario dati: - Valore ritornato: True se l'operazione ha successo, False se il campo specificato da aggiornare non è corretto o come chiave/nuovo nome è stato dato. Nell'aggiornamento del nome, solleva l'eccezione ValueError se si prova a modificare il nome in uno già esistente

Release published by Rikicavaz77: v0.0.1. **Prototipo** iniziale dell'applicativo, sviluppato con il framework _Streamlit_. **Funzionalità** primaria: - _Generazione_ di un prompt. Il **prompt** contiene: - Una _legenda_ dei simboli utilizzati; - Uno schema delle _tabelle rilevanti_, estratte da un dizionario dati raffigurante un database; - La richiesta dell'utente in _linguaggio naturale_. Il prompt generato può essere copiato e incollato su ChatGPT (o altri ChatBOT) per convertire la richiesta dell'utente in una **query SQL**.

Release published by ArjunBasandrai: Elixir v1.0. # Elixir Chess Engine - Initial Release ## Version: 1.0.0 ### Overview Elixir is a UCI-compliant chess engine developed in C++. It is the successor of my previous engine, Shuffle, and is under development with the goal of achieving an ELO rating of 3500+ ### Instructions to install You can install the relevant binaries for your operating system from the `Assets` section located at the bottom of this page ### Instructions to build from source Building Elixir requires `Make` and latest versions of `clang++` or `g++` with `C++20` support ```bash make CXX= ``` - Replace `` with your preferred compiler - either `clang++` or `g++` - If not specified, the compiler defaults to `clang++` - Upon successful compilation, the binary file will appear in the root directory as `elixir` or `elixir.exe` depending on your operating system - You can also give a custom name to the binary by specifying it as `EXE=` during compilation ### Playing Strength Testing with various engines like Integral v1, Stash v21, K2 v0.99 and many others show that the estimated rating of Elixir is ~2800 ELO points ### Feedback and Support If you encounter any issues or have feedback, feel free to create an issue on the project's GitHub repository

Issue closed by GaryJones: Issue with update live blog Entry. Hi Automattic, I have observed a strange behavior in the Liveblog plugin when an update I made to live blog entry. Here is the screenshot. I can see this issue with the latest version as well. Here is the how I can reproduce the issue: * Create An Live blog entry. * Edit the same LiveBlog entry and add extra content to it and update the content. * Now delete the same entry which you have updated. * Now you will see content is deleted without any alert information where we usually get when deleting the content. * Now reload the page. You will see the above screen. So, I have gone through the code and found that we are not checking if an entry exists in the DB. In `liveblog/classes/class-wpcom-liveblog-entry.php` function `get_fields_for_render` Line 97 `$entry_id = $this->replaces ? $this->replaces : $this->comment->comment_ID;` not checking if this`$entry_id` ID exists or not. So I simply added this 2 lines of code in `liveblog/classes/class-wpcom-liveblog-entry.php` function `render` after Line 130 `if ( ! wp_get_comment_status( $entry['entry_id'] ) ) { return $output; }` So that I can only display/loop the file only if an entry ID exists. Hope this will be Helpful, Sorry that I don't have permission to create a PR for this fix.

As of WordPress 4.6, the `comment` cache group is persistent. Thus, after any direct SQL query which `INSERT`s, `UPDATE`s, or `DELETE`s data in comments table, the `clean_comment_cache` function should be called, in order to make the changes immediatelly visible in case a persistent object cache backend (memcache, redis...) is used. This commit also calls the `update_meta_cache` function after direct SQL edits to `commentmeta` table. Fixes #657; REST API routes require a permission_callback; fix: load CPT support later to avoid fatals with early use of WP_Query

Issue closed by GaryJones: 5 consecutive un-renderable WPCOM_Liveblog_Entry items breaks Liveblog. The lazy-loader retrieves entry objects in batches of 5 (or the number dictated by `liveblog_number_of_entries` to a max of 100). Let's call this `$number`. Some retrieved entries may have the property: ``` [replaces] => /**(int)**/ ``` and the additional private property: ``` [type:WPCOM_Liveblog_Entry:private] => delete|update ``` which indicates they are not for display, but are meant to modify another referenced entry. If all `$number` retrieved entries have the `replaces` property, Liveblog may behave unpredictably if it can't render those entires. This is guaranteed to be the case for `delete`, and is sometimes the case for `update` Depending on the circumstances it may: - render none of the retrieved entries (confusing because it appears that the load more action did not work) - fail to load any more entries when "load more" is clicked again. - misrender one or more of the `update` entries in a way that causes it to break entirely for further "load more" clicks. For example, it may fail to find the most recent timestamp in the DOM and begin loading entires from the beginning again, resulting in duplciation This seems broken. It seems like the correct behavior should be to always return `$number` renderable items. These would be entry objects without the `replaces` property, or `replace / update` entries that will result in a valid entry.

Issue closed by GaryJones: Introduce a "Classic" backend editor. ## What's the problem? 1. Liveblog currently maintains it's own React-based editor for the frontend. With the introduction of Gutenberg on the horizon, maintaining a separate editor is inefficient. 1. Adding AMP support to Liveblog was a great addition. Any sites that choose to use an AMP Native theme however don't have a frontend editor, because the AMP format doesn't support that. 1. There have been a number of user requests for years for a backend editor. 1. Users who are not yet ready to make the switch to Gutenberg won't benefit from #594 ## How do we know this is a problem? Through it's experience with clients, WordPress.com VIP has taken lots of feedback about the desire for a backend editor. Some Liveblog users have developed their own solutions, sometimes forking Liveblog in the process which adds an extra maintenance burden for them for features that more users would benefit from. We've spent a lot of time building a React-based editor in order to make the Liveblog editing experience great across mobile as well as desktop. This has added an extra maintenance burden and introduced plenty of bugs. ## What are we doing to solve this problem? Building a classic-based editor to be used on the backend in the WordPress post editor. ## The bet We bet that adding a classic-based editor will: 1. Improve maintainability by re-using the WordPress classic editor. 1. Reduce the burden on users of Liveblog who have decoupled setups or prefer (e.g. for security reasons) to edit on the backend. 1. Provide backwards-compatibility for those users who have not yet switched to Gutenberg. ## What’s the vision? Liveblog users and site owners will be excited to create liveblogs because it's so easy and so familiar. ## Timeline This will be introduced in v2.0, scheduled for release at the end of January 2019. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Users can edit a liveblog from within the post edit screen of the WordPress admin - [ ] The "Key Events" shortcode can be added to the post - [ ] Oembeds (such as Twitter, Facebook etc) should all embed as expected - [ ] Users can mark an entry as a "key event" - [ ] Users can apply a "slash command" to an event - [ ] Each entry can have one or more authors - [ ] The underlying data model remains the same

Pull request opened by charliescheer: Shortcut: Append to note. ### Fix One of the most likely and useful functions we could add to Simplenote shortcuts is the ability to append to a note. So in this PR I have done so. You can setup a shortcut to append a specific content to any note, or you can get the note from another shortcut intent. The append intent uses the simperium api so the server can handle any diffing or sync that needs to happen and the main app does not need to be open for the shortcut to work and then sync. ### Test 1. Build and Run Simplenote, just to make sure that you have saved the extension token so the intents can upload to simperium 2. run the intents extension on the shortcuts app 3. add a new shortcut, find Simplenote, select Append to note 4. add some content and pick a note to append to. Run the shortcut 5. Launch simplenote, find that note, confirm the content was added to the note in question ### Review ***(Required)*** Add instructions for reviewers. For example: > Only one developer is required to review these changes, but anyone can perform the review. ### Release > These changes do not require release notes.

Issue opened by Darxo: [Request] Enforce better skill order. There is a `SkillOrder` system in Vanilla. Every skill gets a number that determines when that skills applies its effective compared to others aswell as how it is sorted into this ui list of actives. In most cases both of those use cases play nice and align. But sometimes we add actives which sneak their way in front of other actives and steal those hotkey positions which can throw off the players muscle memory. One example is the vanilla reload skill which is classified as `::Const.SkillOrder.NonTargeted` but is regularly used by players via hotkeys. - However several utility skills have an earlier Order and will get an earlier position. - Furthermore the Reload skill is usually hidden while not usable, leaving the player to guess, on which hotkey it will spawn. They usually expect it to come directly after the Shoot skill ## Possible Solutions ### Fixed/Favourited Skills Through some kind of UI (Mod Settings?) the player might choose skills which should always be pinned to the front and have priority over non-favourited skills. ### Prioritise Item Skills We could enforce a very common order by giving main/off hand skills priority aswell as moving bag/accessory skills far bag (as those are usually consumable one-time uses and not spammed during battle) > **First** > - Skills from mainhand item > - Skills from offhand item > - All non-item skills > - Skills from bag item > - Skills from accessory > **Last** Then there is some consistency. I think Mainhand and Offhand are the most important and muscle-memoried number hotkeys

Review comment on PR by LordMidas: > We can't put any other operations in that for loop like additional removal or changes of other tooltips. So that whole for loop at that point might aswell be a global utility removeTooltipLine function which takes a tooltip and then up to three additional arguments for id, icon and text. I don't know if we need a helper function for this but maybe it'd be useful. Seems like it is a rather niche use case and if you want to replace multiple entries then it is much more efficient to use a single loop rather than multiple calls to a function like that. > Even still, an incrementing for loop will also fail when a mod adds new global tooltip lines to the getDefaultTooltip function in the skill.nut, with the id 6. I think it is reasonable to say that this is a much less likely scenario than someone adding additional entries to the tooltip of individual skills at the bottom with the id 6. In any case, it doesn't really matter to "pre-emptively optimize" for future potential scenarios. The most stable solution at this point is going to be one with an incrementing loop and if/when we want to remove more entries in the future we can switch to a decrementing one.

Comment on issue by LordMidas: I don't know if there is a reasonable fix for this except that we start putting fullstops within the nested tooltip hyperlink text. However, in this case that'd mean that the entire `Morale.` moves to the next line leaving a large gap up there on the first line which also doesn't look good. Pulling @Enduriel and @TaroEld into the conversation.

Review comment on PR by LordMidas: BB Players don't really understand this so I'd go in a bit more detail: ```squirrel "In vanilla Battle Brothers weapon mastery [perks|Concept.Perk] affect skills, not weapons. So if a Sword/Cleaver hybrid weapon has the [Slash|Skill+slash] skill and the [Decapitate|Skill+decapitate] skill, then [Slash|Skill+slash] benefits from [Sword Mastery|Perk+perk_mastery_sword] and [Decapitate|Skill+decapitate] benefits from [Cleaver Mastery|Perk+perk_mastery_cleaver]. This makes it difficult to work with hybrid weapons. In Reforged, a user requires only one of the applicable masteries of a weapon for all skills of that weapon to fully benefit from mastery effects. So, in the example above, the user would need either [Sword Mastery|Perk+perk_mastery_sword] or [Cleaver Mastery|Perk+perk_mastery_cleaver] and the weapon would behave as if the user had [Sword Mastery|Perk+perk_mastery_sword] for [Slash|Skill+slash] and [Cleaver Mastery|Perk+perk_mastery_cleaver] for [Decapitate|Skill+decapitate].

Release published by LordMidas: 0.5.0-alpha.15. ## CHANGES - Duelist no longer affects AOE attacks. - Longsword: Damage increased from 50-75 to 65-75 and armor ignore from 25% to 30%. - Double gripped swords: now also reduce Fatigue Cost of skills by 33%. - Added unique double grip bonus for fencing sword: +25% armor penetration. - Adjusted SkillOrder of Reload crossbow skills so that they always appear immediately after the shoot skill. - En Garde now never builds Fatigue. Still requires 15 Fatigue remaining. - Meisterhau stance removes the remaining Fatigue requirement from En Garde. - Increased the Reach of Rhomphaia and Warbrand from 5 to 6. - Through the Gaps: reduced armor penetration bonus from +25% to +10%. - Moved Through the Gaps on spear perk group t3 to t2. - Dismemberment: Upon causing an injury, instead of triggering morale checks based on user's Resolve, it triggers them based on HP damage dealt. It always triggers at least 1 morale check and then additional checks for each 33% of HP damage dealt compared to remaining Hitpoints, up to a maximum of 3 morale checks. - Moved Nine Lives from Vigorous to Fast perk group. Moved Survival Instinct from Fast to Vigorous perk group. - Sipar Shield: Reduced Ranged Defense from 15 to 10 and fatigue penalty from -25 to -22. - Improved the tooltip of Tempo to be clearer that it works with hits/misses so that the interaction with AOE attacks is clearer. - Lone Wolf origin now starts with a Greatsword instead of Longsword as we have a different design for the Longsword and the former represents the origin better. - Wardogs and Warhounds can now sometimes be found in the marketplace too, instead of only in Kennels. - Added new names for named Crossbow, Handgonne, Swordlance, Longaxe, Whip. - Changed vanilla named Crossbow name "Betrayer" to be a named Dagger name instead. - Removed Estoc from vanilla named Dagger names as we have our own Estoc weapon. - Reverted the Cost and Strength of Conscripts back to 20 (was recently dropped to 16). - Gladiator: - Removed Skirmisher, Bully and Death Dealer. - Replaced Nimble with Poise. - Re-added Overwhelm. - Moved Pattern Recognition to be only on Champions. - Adjusted the attributes and perks of heavy skeletons: - Praetorian: - Increased XP from 400 to 450. - Reduced Melee Skill from 80 to 75. - Honor Guard: - Reduced Melee Skill from 90 to 80. - Reduced Melee Defense from 20 to 15. - Reduced Ranged Defense from 15 to 0. - Reduced Initiative from 80 to 75. - Both: - Removed Duelist. - Get Exploit Opening with shield. - Get Formidable Approach with 2h weapon. - Get Death Dealer with AOE weapon (e.g. Rhomphaia). ## FIXES - Fixed Dismantle chance calculation being wrong. This was causing it to only be applied when the target completely runs out of armor. - Fixed Vanquisher showing its fatigue affordability preview for invalid tiles instead of valid tiles. - Fixed Regent in Absentia background not properly adding the Family Pride perk to the character and the Noble perk group to the perk tree. - Fixed Weapon Master not properly adding the skills to a character on world screen after game load unless the character unequips/re-equips the weapon. - Fixed errors caused by Kingfisher when moving away from the netted target. - Fixed Kingfisher not properly regaining all skills of the net after the target got "unfished". - Fixed Champion Swordmaster not being able to spawn sometimes. - Fixed Night time effect modifier being shown on attacks even when the night effect wasn't applying to the character. - Fixed typo in rumor text about legendary locations (sweared -> swore). - Fixed squires in noble armies being able to spawn with painted helmets. - Adjusted the RatioMin of the ranged nomad unit block in NomadRoamers party from 0.15 to 0.2 to correspond to the RatioMax of the frontline block of 0.8. ## TECH - Refactored the code in shield.nut to make our changes more moddable. - Added new function `removeValues` to `::MSU.Array` in Reforged's MSU modifications. - Removed unused Misc category from Reforged nested tooltips table. - Fixed instantiating item_container during hooks for populating Reforged nested tooltips concepts. It is now moved to AfterHooks.

Issue opened by Darxo: [Request] Toggle-able concepts. With almost every term having a nested tooltip, tooltips can at times become very busy with many words being underlined and made into a hyperlink. image ### Proposal - Allow the player to toggle on/off certain categories of hyperlinks so they will no longer highlight. - (Alternative) List every single individual nested tooltip in the options page and allow toggling of singular terms Example of categories: - Vanilla Mechanics (Attributes, Turn, Round, Zone of Controls, etc.) - Reforged Mechanics (Reach, Crowded, Stun Threshold?, etc.) - Skills (Effects, Perks, Actives) - Items (Net) ### Thoughts - This idea came to my mind when repeatedly seeing `turn` and `Action Points` being highlighted as hyperlinks. They are such basic concepts that I never feel the need to read up on them ever again. - Most notably I can see veteran players turning off Vanilla Mechanics at some point.

Issue closed by BautistaDalmasso: HHTP response codes incorrectamente usados.. Nuestro Backend envía en varios puntos http responses como `400` para indicar un error generico. * `400`: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/400 * * Tiene que ver con el request en sí estando "mal formado". Por ej: necesita 3 variables y solo se mandaron 2. No se utiliza para errores genéricos del backend. Por ejemplo, si el usuario quiere reservar un libro pero no hay copias de ese libro, la request en sí no tiene nada de malo pero el error viene por otra parte.

type_text: Pull request opened by jdeschamps: Fix transforms. ### Description I erroneously removed the probability of applying transforms from the flips and rotations, leading to a situation where the original patch is never shown to the network. This PR adds the probability parameter back into the transforms. It also adds a new transform that only flips a single axis (as opposed to either X or Y), as this can be useful for particular applications (e.g. cryoCARE). - **What**: Add `p` parameter to transforms, create new `XorYFlip` transform with parameter `flip_x` (`True` for X, `False` for Y). - **Why**: This fixes a problem arising from the transforms always applying, a preventing the original patch to be trained on. - **How**: Parameter is simply added to the existing classes, new class for the `XorYFlip` transform. ### Changes Made - **Added**: `XorYFlip` and `XorYFlipModel`. - **Modified**: `SupportedTransforms`, `XYFlip`, `XYFlipModel`, `XYRandomRotate90`, `XYRandomRotate90Model`, tests. ### Additional Notes and Examples Another way to create the `XorYFlip` transform would have been to add parameters to the existing `XYFlip` to make the flip happen on a single axis. I thought that a `flip_x` (`True` for X, `False` for Y) parameter in a new class is easier for users than asking for an axis value `Optional[Literal[-2, -1]]` to represent the axis to flip in `XYFlip`. Current transform list for flipping only X or Y using `XorYFlip`: ```python transforms = [ NormalizeModel(mean=mean, std=std), XorYFlipModel(flip_x=True), N2VManipulateModel(), ] ``` Potential alternative if implementing it in `XYFlip`: ```python transforms = [ NormalizeModel(mean=mean, std=std), XYFlipModel(axis=-1), # parameters `axis=None` by default to flip both X and Y N2VManipulateModel(), ] ``` Or: ```python transforms = [ NormalizeModel(mean=mean, std=std), XYFlipModel(flip_one_axis=True, flip_x=True), # parameters `flip_one_axis=False` by default to flip both X and Y N2VManipulateModel(), ] ``` Any opinion? --- **Please ensure your PR meets the following requirements:** - [x] Code builds and passes tests locally, including doctests - [x] New tests have been added (for bug fixes/features) - [x] Pre-commit passes - [ ] PR to the documentation exists (for bug fixes / features)

Pull request merged by jdeschamps: Fix transforms. ### Description I erroneously removed the probability of applying transforms from the flips and rotations, leading to a situation where the original patch is never shown to the network. This PR adds the probability parameter back into the transforms. It also adds a new transform that only flips a single axis (as opposed to either X or Y), as this can be useful for particular applications (e.g. cryoCARE). - **What**: Add `p` parameter to transforms, create new `XorYFlip` transform with parameter `flip_x` (`True` for X, `False` for Y). - **Why**: This fixes a problem arising from the transforms always applying, a preventing the original patch to be trained on. - **How**: Parameter is simply added to the existing classes, new class for the `XorYFlip` transform. ### Changes Made - **Added**: `XorYFlip` and `XorYFlipModel`. - **Modified**: `SupportedTransforms`, `XYFlip`, `XYFlipModel`, `XYRandomRotate90`, `XYRandomRotate90Model`, tests. ### Additional Notes and Examples Another way to create the `XorYFlip` transform would have been to add parameters to the existing `XYFlip` to make the flip happen on a single axis. I thought that a `flip_x` (`True` for X, `False` for Y) parameter in a new class is easier for users than asking for an axis value `Optional[Literal[-2, -1]]` to represent the axis to flip in `XYFlip`. Current transform list for flipping only X or Y using `XorYFlip`: ```python transforms = [ NormalizeModel(mean=mean, std=std), XorYFlipModel(flip_x=True), N2VManipulateModel(), ] ``` Potential alternative if implementing it in `XYFlip`: ```python transforms = [ NormalizeModel(mean=mean, std=std), XYFlipModel(axis=-1), # parameters `axis=None` by default to flip both X and Y N2VManipulateModel(), ] ``` Or: ```python transforms = [ NormalizeModel(mean=mean, std=std), XYFlipModel(flip_one_axis=True, flip_x=True), # parameters `flip_one_axis=False` by default to flip both X and Y N2VManipulateModel(), ] ``` Any opinion? --- **Please ensure your PR meets the following requirements:** - [x] Code builds and passes tests locally, including doctests - [x] New tests have been added (for bug fixes/features) - [x] Pre-commit passes - [x] PR to the documentation exists (for bug fixes / features): - https://github.com/CAREamics/careamics.github.io/pull/6 - https://github.com/CAREamics/careamics-examples/pull/1

Pull request opened by jdeschamps: Inputs to BMZ should not be normalized. ### Description The inputs to the BMZ model should not be normalized, as the BMZ core applies the normalization itself. Since all our tests were using tensors with values [-1, 1], this went unnoticed. This PR uses a quick fix by applying denormalization to the patches extracted from the datamodules. This part of the code was refactored into a tested member function of `CAREamist`. I also scaled all tensors in `CAREamit` tests to [0, 255] to be more realistic. - **What**: Add denormalization to BMZ export input data. - **Why**: The current code export normalized tensors, which leads to failing validation of the BMZ archive - **How**: `Denormalize` is now called in a the (refactored) `_create_data_for_bmz` method in `CAREamist`. ### Changes Made - **Added**: `_create_data_for_bmz` method in `CAREamist`, specific tests. - **Modified**: Existing `CAREamist` tests. ### Related Issues Issues reported by users. ### Additional Notes and Examples The choice here is **quick fix** one. The current way example inputs are generated prior to exporting to the BMZ format is by pulling patches from the existing dataloaders (either prediction, or training one): https://github.com/CAREamics/careamics/blob/f613d724fd7e9f8f6ea102ee108701bb44dfae44/src/careamics/careamist.py#L694 This fix here is to simply call `Denormalize` on the array: ```python # unpack a batch, ignore masks or targets input_patch, *_ = next(iter(self.pred_datamodule.predict_dataloader())) # convert torch.Tensor to numpy input_patch = input_patch.numpy() # denormalize denormalize = Denormalize( mean=self.cfg.data_config.mean, std=self.cfg.data_config.std ) input_patch, _ = denormalize(input_patch) ``` An alternative would be to find a way to create a new Dataloader with the data and remove normalization, but this seems possible only after training because the `CAREamist` remembers the source data (unless it is a DataLoader). However, we want to be able to export after loading a checkpoint for instance (choosing best model, loading it, exporting to BMZ). So I think this is the best pragmatic choice. --- **Please ensure your PR meets the following requirements:** - [x] Code builds and passes tests locally, including doctests - [x] New tests have been added (for bug fixes/features) - [x] Pre-commit passes - [x] No change to the documentation needed

The current way example inputs are generated prior to exporting to the BMZ format is by pulling patches from the existing dataloaders (either prediction, or training one): https://github.com/CAREamics/careamics/blob/f613d724fd7e9f8f6ea102ee108701bb44dfae44/src/careamics/careamist.py#L694 This fix here is to simply call `Denormalize` on the array: ```python # unpack a batch, ignore masks or targets input_patch, *_ = next(iter(self.pred_datamodule.predict_dataloader())) # convert torch.Tensor to numpy input_patch = input_patch.numpy() # denormalize denormalize = Denormalize( mean=self.cfg.data_config.mean, std=self.cfg.data_config.std ) input_patch, _ = denormalize(input_patch) ``` An alternative would be to find a way to create a new Dataloader with the data and remove normalization, but this seems possible only after training because the `CAREamist` remembers the source data (unless it is a DataLoader). However, we want to be able to export after loading a checkpoint for instance (choosing best model, loading it, exporting to BMZ). So I think this is the best pragmatic choice. --- **Please ensure your PR meets the following requirements:** - [x] Code builds and passes tests locally, including doctests - [x] New tests have been added (for bug fixes/features) - [x] Pre-commit passes - [x] No change to the documentation needed; (refac): refactor collate and stitching; (chore): add tests for #125; (merge): merge with stitching simplification

Pull request opened by jdeschamps: Add seeds and random number generator. ### Description In order to have more reproducibility when debugging, this PR adds seeds and random number generator to the pixel manipulation and the random patching. This should fix one of the test that is often randomly not passing in the CI. - **What**: Add possibility to fix seed in random patching and pass the random number generator to pixel manipulation. - **Why**: Explain the reasoning behind these changes. What problem are you solving? Why is this change necessary? - **How**: Add `seed` and `rng` (when applicable) to `pixel_manipulation` and `extract_patches_random`. ### Changes Made - **Modified**: Add `seed` and `rng` (when applicable) to `pixel_manipulation` and `extract_patches_random`. ### Related Issues Test randomly not passing in CI. --- **Please ensure your PR meets the following requirements:** - [x] Code builds and passes tests locally, including doctests - [x] New tests have been added (for bug fixes/features) - [x] Pre-commit passes - [x] PR to the documentation exists (for bug fixes / features)

Pull request opened by jdeschamps: Make normalization mandatory. ### Description The current code base applies denormalization automatically (in the prediction step of the `LightningModule` and in the BMZ export), and the datasets all compute the statistics of the data (mean and std). But `Normalization` can be disabled through the Pydantic model! This PR makes `Normalization` mandatory by adding it to the list of transforms directly in the datasets. This simplifies the configuration (no more adding mean/std in two places) and ensures that normalization is always applied. One way to still disable it, is to choose 0 mean and 1 std. - **What**: Make normalization mandatory in the code. - **Why**: Normalization is understood in the code as being always applied, yet it can be disabled through the configuration. - **How**: `Normalization` is removed from the list of transforms and automatically added when creating the `Compose` in the datasets. ### Changes Made - **Modified**: `DataModel`, `SupportedTransforms`, the datasets. - **Removed**: `NormalizationModel` from `DataModel` and `SupportedTransforms`. ### Breaking changes Any code specifically calling `Normalization` in the configuration. --- **Please ensure your PR meets the following requirements:** - [x] Code builds and passes tests locally, including doctests - [x] New tests have been added (for bug fixes/features) - [x] Pre-commit passes - [ ] PR to the documentation exists (for bug fixes / features)

Review comment on PR by OddTomBrooks: I have tried this both ways. In the end, whether by multiple recipients or BCC, the recipient email list is delivered to all recipients. At best, this is inconsistent UX and has a less professional presentation. At worst, there may be some privacy and informational transaction concerns. If we get into multiple thousands of recipients that may be cause for some performance concern, but for the foreseeable future we do not have significant enough scale for this to be a primary concern. At that scale we would need to employ a dispatch service like SES anyway. In conclusion, for the purposes of consistency with other emails and privacy I will maintain this as individually sent emails rather than batching them.

Issue closed by robin-checkmk: [BUG] `discovery` module out of sync with the Checkmk REST API. **Describe the bug** The `discovery` module reports the following error, when run in `bulk_mode`. `fatal: [host -> localhost]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "State 'tabula_rasa' does not exist in bulk_discovery, please use refresh!"}` But this is not true as of now. We have to double-check this. On top of that, with Checkmk 2.3.0 a new approach to service discovery is implemented and while the old options stay for now, they are deprecated. So the bare minimum we need to do, is to fix the above issue. Ideally we directly update the module to use the new options for Checkmk 2.3.0. **Component Name** Component Name: discovery **Ansible Version** ```console $ ansible --version ``` **Checkmk Version and Edition** ```console 2.3.0b3 CRE ``` **Collection Version** ```console $ ansible-galaxy collection list ``` **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Create a task to discover services on a host. 2. Use `tabula_rasa` as the `state`. 3. See the error mentioned above. **Expected behavior** The `discovery` module behaves analogue to the REST API endpoints. **Actual behavior** `fatal: [host -> localhost]: FAILED! => {"changed": false, "msg": "State 'tabula_rasa' does not exist in bulk_discovery, please use refresh!"}` **Minimum reproduction example** ```yaml - name: "Discover services in bulk mode." checkmk.general.discovery: server_url: "{{ server_url }}" site: "{{ site }}" automation_user: "{{ automation_user }}" automation_secret: "{{ automation_secret }}" hosts: "{{ play_hosts }}" bulk_size: 20 state: "tabula_rasa" delegate_to: localhost run_once: true # noqa run-once[task] ``` **Additional context**

type_text: Issue closed by Sbozzolo: Add support for `field_to_array` and `array_to_field`. From ClimaAtmos: ```julia """ field2array(field) Extracts a view of a `ClimaCore` `Field`'s underlying array. Can be used to simplify the process of getting and setting values in an `RRTMGPModel`; e.g. ``` model.center_temperature .= field2array(center_temperature_field) field2array(face_flux_field) .= model.face_flux ``` The dimensions of the resulting array are `([number of vertical nodes], number of horizontal nodes)`. Also, `field` must be a `Field` of scalars, so that the element type of the array is the same as the struct type of `field`. """ function field2array(field::Fields.Field) if sizeof(eltype(field)) != sizeof(eltype(parent(field))) f_axis_size = sizeof(eltype(parent(field))) ÷ sizeof(eltype(field)) error("unable to use field2array because each Field element is \ represented by $f_axis_size array elements (must be 1)") end return data2array(Fields.field_values(field)) end data2array(data::Union{DataLayouts.IF, DataLayouts.IFH}) = reshape(parent(data), :) data2array(data::Union{DataLayouts.IJF, DataLayouts.IJFH}) = reshape(parent(data), :) data2array(data::Union{DataLayouts.VF, DataLayouts.VIFH, DataLayouts.VIJFH}) = reshape(parent(data), size(parent(data), 1), :) """ array2field(array, space) Wraps `array` in a `ClimaCore` `Field` that is defined over `space`. Can be used to simplify the process of getting and setting values in an `RRTMGPModel`; e.g. ``` array2field(model.center_temperature, center_space) .= center_temperature_field face_flux_field .= array2field(model.face_flux, face_space) ``` The dimensions of `array` are assumed to be `([number of vertical nodes], number of horizontal nodes)`. Also, `array` must represent a `Field` of scalars, so that the struct type of the resulting `Field` is the same as the element type of `array`. If this restriction were removed, one would also need to pass the desired `Field` struct type as an argument to `array2field`, which would then need to permute the dimensions of `array` to match the target `DataLayout`. I'm actually a bit flabbergasted that this didn't require MSE changes (https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl/pull/3058). My thoughts on this are one of the following must be true: - This somehow (miraculously) worked due to `Nq`/`Nv` (though I doubt this) - ClimaAtmos' regression tests are insufficient or no longer working as expected (possible, though seems less likely) - The code that seems like it should break badly (below) is not actually executed/exercised (certainly possible) Code that looks like it should break if `Nv` was sent in as `Nq` ```julia Base.IteratorEltype(::Type{Perimeter2D{Nq}}) where {Nq} = Base.HasEltype() Base.eltype(::Type{Perimeter2D{Nq}}) where {Nq} = Tuple{Int, Int} Base.IteratorSize(::Type{Perimeter2D{Nq}}) where {Nq} = Base.HasLength() Base.length(::Perimeter2D{Nq}) where {Nq} = 4 + (Nq - 2) * 4 function Base.iterate(perimeter::Perimeter2D{Nq}, loc = 1) where {Nq} if loc length(perimeter) return (-1, -1) elseif loc <= 4 return vertex_node_index(loc, Nq) else f = cld(loc - 4, Nq - 2) n = mod(loc - 4, Nq - 2) == 0 ? (Nq - 2) : mod(loc - 4, Nq - 2) return face_node_index(f, Nq, 1 + n) end end ``` Regardless, it would be nice if we somehow added tests for `Perimeter2D`. That said, the example that failed is a bit difficult to test precisely because we simply sent in the wrong integer into `Perimeter2D`'s type space. I don't think we should overcomplicate `Perimeter2D` for the sake of testing, but we should be able to somehow test `dss!` to take this into account. cc @sriharshakandala

Issue opened by charleskawczynski: Dispatch logic in `copyto!/fill!` is broken for SubArray's with parent CuArrays. Found by @trontrytel. The CUDA `fill!` is currently defined as: ```julia function Base.fill!( dest::VIJFH{S, Nv, Nij, A}, val, ) where {S, Nv, Nij, A 0 && Nh > 0 Nv_per_block = min(Nv, fld(256, Nij * Nij)) Nv_blocks = cld(Nv, Nv_per_block) auto_launch!( knl_fill!, (dest, val), dest; threads_s = (Nij, Nij, Nv_per_block), blocks_s = (Nh, Nv_blocks), ) end return dest end ``` which doesn't catch when `A <: SubArray{T, N, <:CuArray}`. This seems to be broken/missing in a bunch of places. One scary result of this is that, if it's missed and the CPU version calls `slab` or something, it could result in a huge number of kernel launches (this may actually be happening for some of our gpu jobs).

Issue closed by lucasmarchd01: Contributor changes to a chant after proofreading overwrite proofreading fields. To replicate: - Log in as a proofreader of a source and edit a chant in that source by marking any of the "proofread" checkboxes, or adding someone to the `proofread_by` field, or by specifying a chant range. - Log in as a contributor (ie. someone without proofread access to that source), and then make any edit to the chant. - Log back in as the proofreader and see that all of your changes to those fields (proofread checkboxes, the `proofread_by` field, and the chant range field) have been overwritten. In emails with Debra, it sounds like the following would be preferable: - contributor changes should never overwrite the `proofread_by` or `chant_range` fields - the checkboxes are only "unchecked" by a contributor change if the contributor has actually changed something in one of the related fields ("volpiano proofread" gets unchecked only if the "volpiano" has changed, and so on)

Comment on issue by dchiller: This relates to the series of issues you've created, @ahankinson, but rather than create a meta-issue or discussion, I think it's ok to just discuss this here. Ok, so here's what I understand to be the current state of affairs and some of the problems: `title` (current city + current archive + shelfmark), a `siglum` (institution siglum + shelfmark), and a pointer to the `RismSiglum` model (intended to be the "RISM" -- ie. institutional -- siglum). The "RISM" sigla (quotes intentional) used in both the source's `siglum` and `RismSiglum` are not always accurate. The `siglum` and `RismSiglum` fields can be modified independently, as can the title. It's kinda a mess. There's currently no linkage between sources in CantusDB and other catalogs, etc (e.g. RISM, the institution's own record, etc.) If I'm understanding this set of issues (1505 - 1509), the goal is to standardize and enhance source identification in the following ways: - get rid of the `RismSiglum` table and associated fields -- they are not accurate (and also, frankly, not really used) - create an `Institution` model that contains information (`name`, `siglum`, `city`) on the institutions that hold our sources - create an `InstitutionIdentifier` model that contains various ID's for the institutions in `Institution`. For example, for the there might be multiple records in Instititution Identifier model that point to the Bodleian (for example, both BNF cb11930727f and RISM institutions/30001627 - create a `SourceIdentifier` model that does basically the same thing as `InstitutionIdentifier` but at the source-level. _Questions_ 1. Is `Institution.siglum` a RISM siglum or a CantusDB siglum? 2. Is `shelfmark` a `SourceIdenfier`? Or maybe we still store that directly on the source itself?

Issue opened by annamorphism: some IDs make create-chant break?. I just got an email from an indexer who had created the first chant in a source, but got a 500 error when trying to add a second. I tried myself and also can't seem to add a new chant to https://cantusdatabase.org/source/1000051. When I created a chant with identical information in a test source, it also gave me a 500 error, but added the chant to the source. When I then tried to add new chants to the test source, it gave a 500. Remove the new chant--> can create as normal. I tried removing the content in various fields in the new chant, and strangely, deleting or replacing the Cantus ID seemed to solve the problem. Why would the ID g00791 be making it so you can't create a new chant in that source? Further investigation required.

Comment on issue by ahankinson: There is a terminology issue here that’s been known since the migration but hasn’t yet been addressed. See: https://github.com/DDMAL/CantusDB/issues/621 Basically, the word “siglum” can mean “shelfmark” in some musicological circles, but this creates confusion when talking about “RISM sigla”. Institution.siglum is a RISM siglum: GB-Ob, D-Mbs, etc. In an ideal world the Source “siglum” column would be renamed “shelfmark” when the institution component of that is removed and ladder in through its relationship to a holding institution. That’s how it is in DIAMM. But I didn’t want to tackle that just yet, since that’s more a project terminology question, and there’s no technical reason to change it. Source Identifiers are like institution identifiers, where multiple places may publish a page on the source: wikidata, bnf, RISM, etc. It will operate exactly like the institution identifiers.

Comment on issue by dchiller: > Institution.siglum is a RISM siglum: GB-Ob, D-Mbs, etc. So, in cases where a source is held by an "institution" without a RISM siglum...I guess this is a place where the current `source.siglum` would hold some kind of identifier to a source's holding location, but that source would not point to an `Institution`.

Comment on issue by ahankinson: That was what we were trying to figure out in the email. I think what we landed on was that sources not held by institutions with a RISM siglum would be “held” by a Cantus institution with its own RISM siglum — CDN-WAcantus or something like that. All sources should have a holding institution, and that should be the only place institution sigla are catalogued. What the shelfmark is for such sources, however, is still TBD. It could include a geographic indicator, but I have suggested that this isn’t ideal for privacy reasons. That’s a problem for future us at the moment though.

Issue opened by annamorphism: should users get an email when they have an account created?. I believe on OldCantus there was an option Debras could check when creating a user that would send an email notifying them that they now had a Cantus account. I don't think such an option exists anymore, so Debras have to then email users to let them know that their account exists and that they should try logging in, changing their password, etc. Is that the case? And if it is the case, is that by design? (It doesn't seem like a big problem, since by definition there has already been some conversation requesting the account...)

Comment on issue by dchiller: Ok... this is interesting. When the suggested chants function starts looking for the next chants after `g00791`, Cantus Index responds with the following top three Cantus ID's: - 'g00791a ' - 'g00711' - 'g01957' Note that the first ID has a trailing space. When the function then asks for the data on each of these ID's, the inclusion of the space in the case of the first ID causes Cantus Index to respond with all of the chants in the Cantus network with that Cantus ID (in other words, all the concordances) but crucially not the metadata for that Cantus ID (i.e. the full text, the genre, etc.) that we use to populate the chant suggestion on CantusDB. So: 1. Cantus Index is returning that slightly mal-formed Cantus ID, and then 2. It can use that Cantus ID to return a response (and thus not triggering CantusDB's built-in error handling) but not the elements of the response we are expecting (thus triggering a 500 error). We should make our suggested chants feature more robust to this error. But also, what's going on with this CantusID in Cantus Index?
Comment on issue by dchiller: > But also, what's going on with this CantusID in Cantus Index? @annamorphism Do you have access to see whether this spacing was perhaps an entry error in Cantus Index?

Review comment on PR by NMertsch: I agree. Pydantic can support us in two major ways: 1. Represent and work with data in a structured way (as BaseModels) instead of hacking around with nested dicts and lists. 2. Convert data between JSON strings and Python objects. If we only want the JSON de-/serialization, having huge `model_validator`s a valid the solution: We can do all the hacky `dict` magic we want, and in the end we get a `BaseModel` instance. Pydantic also offers some tools to perform transformations in a more structured way: - computed_field to create new fields based on parsed data - exclude to exclude fields during serialization - aliases to automatically rename fields - Enum parsing to avoid "magic strings" [Click me] Example from the Pretix API ```python from enum import Enum from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field class PretixOrderStatus(Enum): PAID = "p" PENDING = "n" EXPIRED = "e" CANCELED = "c" class PretixOrderPosition(BaseModel): order_id: str = Field(alias="order") item_id: int = Field(alias="item") attendee_name: str | None class PretixOrder(BaseModel): id: str = Field(alias="code") status: PretixOrderStatus = Field(exclude=True) positions: list[PretixOrderPosition] @computed_field def is_paid(self) -> bool: return self.status is PretixOrderStatus.PAID order_json = """ { "code": "ABC01", "status": "p", "positions": [ { "order": "ABC01", "item": 123, "attendee_name": "Jane Doe" }, { "order": "ABC01", "item": 234, "attendee_name": "John Doe" } ] } """ order = PretixOrder.model_validate_json(order_json) assert order.model_dump_json(indent=2) == """\ { "id": "ABC01", "positions": [ { "order_id": "ABC01", "item_id": 123, "attendee_name": "Jane Doe" }, { "order_id": "ABC01", "item_id": 234, "attendee_name": "John Doe" } ], "is_paid": true }""" ``` I know this is a matter of opinion, feel free to keep the code as it is. PS: `BaseModel.parse_raw` is deprecated in Pydantic v2, please use `BaseModel.model_validate_json` instead 🙂

Temporal relationship between submissions > I would prefer to store the relationships (parallel, before, after, next, previous) in a separate data structure which references these `PretalxSubmission` objects. > Then we wouldn't have this situation where creating a "complete" `PretalxSubmission` object requires to steps: ```python submission = PretalxSubmission(...) # call `__init__`, which only initialized a part of the object submission.set_talks_in_parallel(...) # initialize another part of the object submission.set_talks_after(...) # initialize yet another part of the object [...] ``` > Field like `talks_in_parallel: list[str] | None = None` can easily cause to accidents: `my_submission.talks_in_parallel` *sometimes* contains the "talks in parallel to my submission", depending on *when* I access the field. > That would be a non-trivial change, and the current implementation seems to work, so I'm fine with merging it as it is. Issue closed by sosnovsky: Pressing "Enter" twice in beginning/endings of quoted text required before a newline actually rendered. Description: It was reported to us that it requires them to press the "Enter" on their keyboard twice before a newline to render. Upon further investigation, the issue exists when interacting onto the beginning or endings of the quoted text. To be specific, its on the the line where the "On , wrote:" starts or at the last occuring line of the quoted text "> some quoted text...". Steps to reproduce: 1. Open Gmail with FlowCrypt browser extension set up. 2. Open any FlowCrypt-renderable emails (encrypted+signed or signed) in your inbox. 3. Click on "Secure Reply". 4. Click onto the "..." icon button on the bottom part of the Secure reply box to see the quoted email text. 5. On the section "On , wrote:" or at the last occuring line of the quoted text "> some quoted text...", try to press Enter and you'll not be getting an expected newline. It will require you to press Enter twice for a newline to be inserted. Reference: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/human@flowcrypt.com/#inbox/QgrcJHsbjBtCThLpRmNDcjlkLmVBPrQHhVB

Issue closed by johscheuer: Using the same monitor conf for different storage server densities on the new image. We currently customize the monitor conf for the unified image with different flags based on how many storage servers we are running per disk. This adds some complexity, because we have to switch between different entries in the config map when we are changing the storage server density. On the old image, we were specifying multiple command lines when running multiple storage servers, but that's not the case on the new image, so we should be able to move to using the same monitor conf regardless of storage server density.

Bumps the lib group with 11 updates in the /frontend/lib directory: Updates `@reduxjs/toolkit` from 2.2.3 to 2.2.5 Release notes Sourced from @​reduxjs/toolkit's releases. v2.2.5 This bugfix release fixes an issue in the recent createEntityAdapter sorting perf improvements that could (in specific cases) cause Immer to throw an error when trying to read a plain JS value instead of a proxy-wrapped value. What's Changed Fix missed spot where use of current may fail if the value is not a draft by @​markerikson in reduxjs/redux-toolkit#4412 Full Changelog: https://github.com/reduxjs/redux-toolkit/compare/v2.2.4...v2.2.5 v2.2.4 This bugfix release improves sorting performance in createEntityAdapter, shrinks the code size in matcher utilities, fixes assorted issues with query hooks, and makes several TS tweaks. Changelog Entity Adapter Sorting Performance Users reported in #4252 that the sorting performance of createEntityAdapter seemed abnormally bad - the provided comparison functions were being called far more times than expected. Upon investigation, we had a couple of problems. We were always starting from an array that was in insertion order, not the existing sorted order, and that would always require significant effort to re-sort even if there weren't any actual changes to the sorted results. Also, the sorting checks required frequent access to Immer's Proxy-wrapped values, even in cases where all we needed was the plain state values for comparison purposes. We've reworked the internal sorting logic to always start from the existing sorted array, do reads against a plain value to avoid the Proxy getter overhead where possible, and optimized inserts into existing sorted arrays. This should significantly speed up sorted entity adapter behavior. Matcher Code Size Optimization We've reworked the internals of the thunk-related matchers to deduplicate some of the logic, shaving a few bytes off the final bundle size. RTK Query Hook Updates defaultSerializeQueryArgs can now handle BigInt values safely. The isLoading flag logic was improved to handle errors when a query hook tries to subscribe. TS Updates create.asyncThunk's types were improved to avoid cases where it might infer any. We've made several internal types changes to work correctly with React 19's upcoming types. The retryCondition method now receives unknown as an argument, instead of always assuming the user is using fetchBaseQuery. Other Changes The Reselect dep has been bumped to 5.1.0 to match the expected internal usage of createSelector.withTypes(). Issue opened by dtrucs: Display JSON feeds (blog posts, news, etc.) as cards from another website. If you want to display articles from another website, you can do so using custom HTML templates. ## Demo Screenshot image ## JSON Feed To retrieve data from another website, the well-known feeds are RSS or Atom, but the best format for communicating remains JSON, so we decided to develop a script that uses them all: JSON Feed. So, if you wish to copy/paste the following codes into your customization but with your own feed, it must be formatted in JSON Feed or you must edit the following script to adapt it. ## Template ### Common Let's try the following code and copy it into a template file like `customization/html/homeTop.html`: ```html ``` - `data-widget="feed"` (mandatory): all HTML tags with this data attribute and the value “feed” will be parsed by the corresponding script. - `data-url` (mandatory): this is the feed source. If left blank, nothing happens. - `data-limit` (optional - default `Infinity`): is the number of elements to be displayed. - `data-title` (optional): allows to add a title to the section ### Internationalization If the feed is only available in one language, we suggest you paste it only in the suffixed template: `homeTop-en.html`. If you have feeds available in different languages, you can duplicate the template with the language code as a suffix as above, or you can use the `{{ language }}` variable. Using the HTML example above, let's assume that JSON feeds are available via these urls `https://www.ecrins-parcnational.fr/en/flux_actus.json` for the English version and `https://www.ecrins-parcnational.fr/fr/flux_actus.json` for the French version. You can therefore only define `homeTop.html` with the following content: ```html ``` ### Widget in details page It works in the same way. You can create the file `customization/html/details/feedWidget.html` and paste the following template: ```html ``` Don't forget to call the `feedWidget` in the desired details page in `customization/config/details.json`. ```json { "sections": { "trek": [ { "name": "feedWidget", "display": true, "anchor": true, "order": 200 } ] } } ``` The main difference with the common template is that you don't have to define the `data-title` attribute, as the title is automatically defined in translated files under the key `details.[file-widget-name]`. For example, in `customization/translations/en.json` : ```diff { + "details": { + "feedWidget": "Actualités" + } } ``` ## Script: All this won't work without the associated script. You can copy/paste the script below into `customization/html/scriptsHeader.html`: ```js async function getFeedContent(url) { const storageUrl = 'feedWidget:' + url; if (window[storageUrl]) { return window[storageUrl]; } if (!url) return null; try { const feedContent = await fetch(url).then(response => response.json()); window[storageUrl] = feedContent; return feedContent; } catch { return null; } } async function generateFeedTemplate(Widget) { const { dataset: { url, limit = 'Infinity', title }, } = Widget; Widget.classList.add('empty:hidden'); const rawfeed = await getFeedContent(url); if (!rawfeed) return; // JSONFeed format const feed = Array.isArray(rawfeed) ? rawfeed : rawfeed.items; if (feed.length === 0) return; const Title = title && Object.assign(document.createElement('h3'), { className: 'mb-2 desktop:mb-6 text-H2 desktop:text-H2 font-bold', textContent: title, }); const List = Object.assign(document.createElement('ul'), { className: 'flex items-start gap-4 desktop:gap-6 overflow-x-auto overflow-y-hidden scroll-smooth snap-x pb-5 mt-4 mb-2', }); feed.slice(0, limit).forEach(item => { const Item = Object.assign(document.createElement('li'), { className: 'relative border border-solid border-greySoft rounded-lg flex-none mx-1 overflow-hidden hover:border-blackSemiTransparent transition duration-500 w-70', }); const image = item.image ?? item.banner_image; const ItemImg = image && Object.assign(document.createElement('img'), { loading: 'lazy', src: item.image ?? item.banner_image, className: 'overflow-hidden size-full object-cover object-center', alt: '', }); const ItemContent = Object.assign(document.createElement('div'), { className: 'flex flex-col gap-2 p-4', }); const ItemTitle = Object.assign(document.createElement('h4'), { className: 'text-xl', }); const ItemLink = Object.assign(document.createElement('a'), { className: "text-primary1 hover:text-primary3 focus:text-primary3 before:content-[''] before:absolute before:inset-0", href: item.url, target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener noreferrer', textContent: item.title, }); const date = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(document.documentElement.lang).format( new Date(item.date_published), ); const summary = item.summary ?? item.content_text; let ItemSummary = summary ? Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { className: 'line-clamp-2 desktop:line-clamp-5', textContent: date + ' - ' + (item.summary ?? item.content_text), }) : Object.assign(document.createElement('div'), { className: 'content-WYSIWYG line-clamp-2 desktop:line-clamp-5', innerHTML: date + item.content_html, }); ItemTitle.append(ItemLink); ItemContent.append(ItemTitle, ItemSummary); ItemImg && Item.append(ItemImg); Item.append(ItemContent); List.append(Item); }); Title && Widget.append(Title); Widget.append(List); } function initFeedWidget() { window.setTimeout(() => { Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-widget="feed"]'), generateFeedTemplate); }, 200); } // Wait for the load of next router const routeChange = setInterval(async function () { if (window.next && window.next.router) { window.next.router.events.on('routeChangeComplete', initFeedWidget); initFeedWidget(); clearInterval(routeChange); } }, 100); ``` A few explanations about the script: - The first action is to add a `className` to the template in order to hide it if it is empty. - If there is no `data-url` defined, or if there is an error when retrieving the data, or if the data returns 0 elements, the script stops execution and nothing is displayed. - The source URL must provide a JSON feed format, otherwise it will try to loop inside as if the response were the contents of the `items` key of the JSON feed. **No other checks are made**, so if your JSON is not properly formatted, errors may occur. - For the card content, it tries to get the value of `summary`, if this key has no value, it tries the value of `content_text`. And if this key also has no value, it finally tries with `content_html`. Be careful with the last property: you have to trust the source because it executes a `innerHTML`.

type_text: Issue closed by dlaliberte: Keyboard accessibility issues with nested sltree. Loading https://webstatus.dev/ and hitting TAB repeatedly ends us cycling between two items in the sidebar, both of which get two tab stops. Focusing something else like the search field and tabbing through eventually cycles around to the same place and gets stuck in the sidebar menu.

Visiting say https://webstatus.dev/features/popover and clicking on various points in the chart produces nice little tooltips with stats. However, if you keep clicking on other points the tooltip isn't being reset, it just accumulates the details of what you click: Screenshot 2024-05-22 8 37 35 AM

Pull request merged by dlaliberte: Restructure layout of Feature header and controls. This PR just restructures the layout of header and control elements on the Feature detail page to allow for different widths of the screen. * The summary boxes are given equal width, which is adaptive to the screen width. This fixes #275. * The links to wpt.fyi and caniuse are moved to the top as peers of the breadcrumbs. TODO: the widths are too much for the mobile mode, since I use @media which is only sensitive to the screen width rather than the container width. Using @container wasn't working as expected for me, so more experimentation will be required.

Issue opened by jcscottiii: Leverage cache for devcontainer. The majority of the time for the GitHub actions is because we rebuild the devcontainer every time. This is very expensive and can lead to a lot of machine-hours. Instead, we should cache the devcontainer as mentioned in this GitHub action: https://github.com/devcontainers/ci - [ ] Have a new workflow that runs weekly (or run manually) that publishes the artifact - [ ] Have the existing workflows use the cache - [ ] Only keep the last 3/N images to prevent using too much space in the GitHub Org. - [ ] Bonus: Have the local development use the same published artifact to reduce local start up time too

Comment on issue by foolip: That being said, I guess that zero people depend on the aliases that we have so far. It might be a good idea to just remove all of them and not claim those identifiers forever. I'm sure we'll eventually need to support redirects for mistakes and merged features, however.

Issue opened by dlaliberte: Preserve date range between pages?. The default date range on the Feature details page is the previous year, but if a different date range would make more sense for some users or some features, there is no easy way to preserve a change in the date range across features. The stats page will also have a date range setting, and the Feature overview page also effectively has a date range in the form of the filter options. Bookmarking a set of filters would therefore be one way of preserving and restoring a date range setting, at least for the Feature overview page. * Should these date ranges be shared between pages? * Should we have some convenience controls for setting the date range to various preset values?

Issue opened by dlaliberte: Use grid layout to simplify layout. The flex box layout we are using now has a few deficiencies in some cases which require arbitrary fixed percentages along with @media or @container queries to constrain the sizes of various components. Grid layout css might work better in these situations.

Comment on issue by Hacksore: It's def possible technically, here is a quick PoC of using discord-rpc. This requires the scope to be expanded to include `messages.read` which is a bit spooky 😂. https://github.com/Hacksore/overlayed/assets/996134/1f58cc73-7f07-4811-ace5-de5bbe6e7820 Code for refrence. ```js const RPC = require("discord-rpc"); const client = new RPC.Client({ transport: "ipc" }); // NOTE: overlayed app id const clientId = "905987126099836938"; // NOTE: overlayed app secret const clientSecret = process.env.CLIENT_SECRET; client.on("ready", () => { console.log("Authed for user", client.user); // sub to a channel for messages client.subscribe("MESSAGE_CREATE", { channel_id: "1125834408356757554", }); }); client.on("MESSAGE_CREATE", (data) => { const { nick, content } = data.message; console.log(`${nick}: ${content}`); }); // Log in to RPC with access token client.login({ clientId, clientSecret, redirectUri: "http://localhost", scopes: ["rpc", "messages.read"], }); ```

Pull request merged by IgnacioBarraza: Feat/add gallery route handler. # Añadir una ruta para interactuar con la tabla 'gallery' ## ¿Por qué se hizo? 🥸 🔗 Jira ## ¿Qué se hizo? 🪚 Se creó una nueva ruta en el servidor que permite leer/crear/actualizar/eliminar registros en la tabla 'gallery' de la base de datos. ## ¿Cómo se prueba esto? 🧪 1. `npm run dev` en el backend. 2. Hacer una petición en Postman para loguearse y copiar el token generado. 3. Crear una petición GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/gallery/`. Pegar el token en el header: `Bearer ${token}`. Si todo va bien, debería devolver un array de objetos correspondientes a los datos de la tabla 'gallery'. 4. Crear una petición POST a `http://localhost:3000/api/gallery/new`, pergar el token en los headers e incluir lo siguiente como body: ```JSON { "id_servicios": "['897b3c23-03e1-44c9-8cc3-88f8bd5fd57a', 'b9331722-cdc5-43b4-8651-eccf117e34b8']", "imagen_link": "https://ibb.co/Lz6qK4W" } ``` El campo `id_servicios` puede aceptar un array de ids. Si todo funciona correctamente, se debería devolver el mensaje 'La imagen se ha agregado con éxito.' 5. Crear una petición PUT a `http://localhost:3000/api/gallery/update/id-imagen-tabla-gallery` y pegar el token en los headers. Se le pueden pasar los campos `id_servicios` o `imagen_link`. Ten en cuenta que `id_servicio` debe existir en la base de datos. ```JSON { "id_servicios": "['b9331722-cdc5-43b4-8651-eccf117e34b8']", "imagen_link": "link-nueva-imagen" } ``` Si todo va bien, se debería devolver el mensaje 'Los datos de la imagen se han actualizado con éxito.' 6. Crear una petición DELETE a `http://localhost:3000/api/gallery/delete/id-imagen-tabla-gallery`, pegar el token en los headers. Si todo funciona correctamente, la imagen se debería eliminar de la galería.

Pull request merged by IgnacioBarraza: Refactor/migrate product router to service router. # Cambiar el route handler de producto por el de servicio ## ¿Por qué se hizo? 🥸 Se actualizó la base de datos y ahora, en lugar de tener la tabla 'producto', está la tabla 'servicios'. El servidor tiene que estar actualizado conforme a la database para poder realizar operaciones en ella. ## ¿Qué se hizo? 🪚 Se borraron las rutas y los esquemas relacionados con la tabla de producto y se añadió una ruta y un esquema para la tabla de servicios. ## ¿Cómo se prueba esto? 🧪 1. `npm run dev` en la carpeta backend. 2. Hacer una petición en Postman para loguearse con credenciales correctas y copia el token. 3. Crea una petición en Postman de tipo GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/service/` y pega el token en los headers. Authorizarion: Bearer `token-aqui`. Debería devolver un array de objetos. 4. Crea una petición en Postman de tipo POST a `http://localhost:3000/api/service/new` y pega el token en los headers igual que con el paso anterior. Puedes pasarle los campos `nombre`, `precio`, `descripcion` (obligatoios) e `imagen` (opcional): ```JSON { "nombre": "Manejo de redes sociales extendido 2", "precio": 75000, "descripcion": "3 semanas de manejo de redes sociales, historias y publicaciones", "imagen": "['https://ibb.co/kxdJkCd']" } ``` Si todo funciona correctamente, se debería crear ese recurso en la base de datos y el servidor debería devolver el mensaje "Servicio creado!". 5. Crea una petición en Postman de tipo PUT a `http://localhost:3000/api/service/new/id-de-un-servicio` y pega el token en los headers. Puedes pasarle algunos o todos los parámetros que se deseen actualizar. Si todo va bien, el recurso se debería actualizar en la base de datos y el servidor debería devolver el mensaje "Servicio actualizado!". 6. Crea una petición en Postman de tipo DELETE a `http://localhost:3000/api/service/delete/id-del-servicio` y pegar el token en los headers. Si todo va bien, el recurso se debería eliminar de la base de datos y el servidor debería devolver el mensaje "Servicio eliminado correctamente!". ◕‿◕

Pull request merged by IgnacioBarraza: Feat/add shopping cart logic. # Añadir lógica para el carrito de compras ## ¿Por qué se hizo? 🥸 🔗 Jira ## ¿Qué se hizo? 🪚 Se creó una nueva ruta que permite leer/crear/actualizar/eliminar registros en la tabla `shopping cart` de la base de datos. ## ¿Cómo se prueba esto? 🧪 1. `npm i` y `npm run dev` en el backend. 2. Hacer una petición en Postman para loguearse y copiar el token generado. 3. Crear una petición GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/cart`. Pegar el token en el header: `Bearer ${token}`. Si todo va bien, debería devolver un array de objetos correspondientes a los datos de la tabla 'gallery'. 4. Crear una petición POST a `http://localhost:3000/api/cart/new`, pergar el token en los headers e incluir lo siguiente como body: ```JSON { "id_usuario": "id-de-usuario-existente", "valor_total": 75000, "id_servicios": "['b9331722-cdc5-43b4-8651-eccf117e34b8']" } ``` El campo `id_servicios` puede aceptar un array de ids. Si todo funciona correctamente, se debería devolver el mensaje 'Orden guardada con éxito!.' 5. Crear una petición PUT a `http://localhost:3000/api/cart/update/id-shopping-cart` y pegar el token en los headers. Los campos son opcionales. Ten en cuenta que `id_usuario` debe existir en la base de datos. ```JSON { "valor_total": 80000, "id_usuario": "id-de-usuario-valida-(36 caracteres)" } ``` Si todo va bien, se debería devolver el mensaje 'Orden actualizada!' 6. Crear una petición DELETE a `http://localhost:3000/api/cart/delete/id-shopping-cart`, pegar el token en los headers. Si todo funciona correctamente, la imagen se debería eliminar de la galería y el servidor debería devolver el mensaje 'La orden se ha eliminado con éxito.'

Pull request opened by JoelFaldin: Refactor/update inventory logic. # Actualizar lógica del inventario ## ¿Por qué se hizo? 🥸 🔗 Jira ## ¿Qué se hizo? 🪚 Se actualizaron las rutas en el backend correspondientes a la interacción con la tabla 'inventario', para que concuerden con las columnas de la nueva database. ## ¿Cómo se prueba esto? 🧪 1. `npm i` y `npm run dev` en la carpeta `backend`. 2. Hacer una petición para loguearse con los datos de un usuario de tipo 'admin' y copiar el token generado. 3. Hacer una petición tipo GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/` y pegar el token en los headers. `Bearer ${token-aqui}`. Debería devolver un array con los registros de la tabla `inventario`. 4. Hacer una petición tipo POST a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/new`, pegar el token en los headers como se hizo anteriormente y pasarle datos en el body: ```JSON { "nombre": "test", "id_equipos": "['111', '112']", "id_servicios": "['1111']" } ``` Si todo va bien, se debería crear el dato en la base de datos y el servidor debería devolver el mensaje 'Inventario creado!'. 5. Hacer una petición tipo PUT a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/update/${id-de-un-dato-existente}`, pegar el token en los headers como se hizo anteriormente y pasarle cualquiera de los 3 datos (nombre_inventario, id_equipos o id_servicios). ```JSON { "nombre": "test2" } ``` Si todo funciona bien, se debería actualizar el dato en la base de datos. 6. Hacer una petición tipo DELETE a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/delete/${id-de-un-dato-existente}` y pegar el token en los headers. Si todo va bien, se debería eliminar el dato.

Hacer una petición GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/get/services` sin poner el token en los headers. Debería devolver un array de objetos con datos de la base de datos. 3. Hacer una petición GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/get/gallery` sin poner el token en los headers, debería devolver un array vacío (porque no hay datos en esa tabla). De todas maneras, si se agregan datos, deberían aparecer ahí. 4. Hacer una petición GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/get/inventory` sin agregar el token. Igual que en la anterior, debería devolver un array vacío porque no hay datos en esa tabla, y si se agregan datos, deberían aparecer ahí.

Pull request merged by IgnacioBarraza: Refactor/update inventory logic. # Actualizar lógica del inventario ## ¿Por qué se hizo? 🥸 🔗 Jira ISSUE ## ¿Qué se hizo? 🪚 Se actualizaron las rutas en el backend correspondientes a la interacción con la tabla 'inventario', para que concuerden con las columnas de la nueva database. ## ¿Cómo se prueba esto? 🧪 1. `npm i` y `npm run dev` en la carpeta `backend`. 2. Hacer una petición para loguearse con los datos de un usuario de tipo 'admin' y copiar el token generado. 3. Hacer una petición tipo GET a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/` y pegar el token en los headers. `Bearer ${token-aqui}`. Debería devolver un array con los registros de la tabla `inventario`. 4. Hacer una petición tipo POST a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/new`, pegar el token en los headers como se hizo anteriormente y pasarle datos en el body: ```JSON { "nombre": "test", "id_equipos": "['111', '112']", "id_servicios": "['1111']" } ``` Si todo va bien, se debería crear el dato en la base de datos y el servidor debería devolver el mensaje 'Inventario creado!'. 5. Hacer una petición tipo PUT a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/update/${id-de-un-dato-existente}`, pegar el token en los headers como se hizo anteriormente y pasarle cualquiera de los 3 datos (nombre_inventario, id_equipos o id_servicios). ```JSON { "nombre": "test2" } ``` Si todo funciona bien, se debería actualizar el dato en la base de datos. 6. Hacer una petición tipo DELETE a `http://localhost:3000/api/inventory/delete/${id-de-un-dato-existente}` y pegar el token en los headers. Si todo va bien, se debería eliminar el dato.

Review comment on PR by davidorme: My feeling is that the auto-profiling is becoming more of a barrier to progress than an asset. There doesn't seem to be a good, minimally intrusive way of implementing this and we are getting profiling failures on PRs that don't affect the code. My guess is that this is some combination of the particular runner and the load being small enough to get frequent stochastic differences. I honestly think we should dump the automatic profiling on PRs for now because: * it is fouling up our PRs, * doesn't look feasible as we want it to run, and * is unreliable. We can re-use the code - maybe at another point? I think a manual process is probably easier - but we could try and generate a comparison (on the same runner) between a new release and its predecessor. That runs the risk of interfering with the trusted publishing though. Do any other projects do this kind of thing (successfully!).

Review comment on PR by davidorme: In the short term, I'm not inclined to hold up `1.0.0` while we iron this out - it's a developer facing issue that doesn't affect the release of the new functionality.

Issue opened by davidorme: Simplify the `jupyter kernelspec` setup. **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** We currently manually set up an explicit `jupyter` kernel specification used to specify the python kernel used in `jupyter` notebooks. This was a way of ensuring that the `jupyter` environment was consistent across developers, runners etc, despite the machine specific `poetry` environment names. However `poetry shell` and `poetry run` now (or possibly _always did_) automatically adjust the `'jupyter` kernels to point `python3` to the active `poetry` virtual environment. Review comment on PR by AmyOctoCat: Thanks David, it's really good to see an illustration of what you meant. I'm a bit concerned that when adding and removing cohorts we'd have to be very careful to ensure that we removed the relevant entries from every set of traits, ie all the t model geometries, all the community traits, etc., since if we missed one, we'd end up with the data misaligned, which might make it a bit fragile. If we later added new attributes to a cohort, then we'd also need to be sure we were adding them into whatever function we use to remove/add them. The best case would be the arrays being different lengths and ending up with a runtime failure, but I'd also be worried about the program silently just attaching the wrong geometry to the wrong cohort etc (for example if we removed one cohort from one data set and a different one from another).

It is possible though that adding and deleting cohorts is much more efficient with lists of `Cohort` instances than subsetting and appending arrays? > > 2. I think I'd rather have factory methods of classes than the intermediate import classes - it just seems cleaner. Hi David, Thank you very much for the feedback, these were things I was going round in circles a bit myself, so it's great to have the input. Regarding the first point I think I've circled round on the arrays vs objects quite a few times over and still don't have a strong feeling. I think going for the OO approach might make it easier to read and easier to reason about when it comes to adding and removing cohorts, but I can see the efficiency argument for using arrays. Regarding the second point I also went in and out on this. JSON dataclasses did not play very nicely with passing the flora object into the nested cohorts within the community which was why I ended up with the separate import classes (I thought this was also a bit clearer from the point of view of easily seeing which fields were needed in the input data). Once there were separate import classes, the logic looked quite complicated and I thought it deserved it's own class (was going for the single responsibility principle from SOLID), but will have a review to see if there's a better way. Maybe adding extra functionality to the generated from_json method that json_dataclass creates in the cohort class is possible that would allow us to pass the flora in there. Sorry that's all very inconclusive! Hopefully some more ideas might percolate over the space of the weekend.

Code pushed by jorisdral: Interim function for loading tables from disk This is a temporary addition to the public API, which we will use until we have properly implemented snapshotting. The intended usage is to first request `listRunNames` from a table handle. This returns a set of paths, and the structure determines which runs live on which levels. One can then pass these paths to `open'` to open the runs from disk, fully verifying the files for each run. `open'` should be exception-safe, in the sense that it ensures no file resources are leaked, even when some runs may have been opened already before an exception is raised.

Code pushed by jorisdral: Interim function for loading tables from disk This is a temporary addition to the public API, which we will use until we have properly implemented snapshotting. The intended usage is to first request `snapshot'` from a table handle. This returns a set of paths, and the structure determines which runs live on which levels. One can then pass these paths to `open'` to open the runs from disk, fully verifying the files for each run. Note that the writebuffer is persisted to disk as a run when using `snapshot'`. The original table remains unchanged. `open'` should be exception-safe, in the sense that it ensures no file resources are leaked, even when some runs may have been opened already before an exception is raised.

Issue closed by juliohm: Implement ringequal for polygons and closed chains. I just figured out that the sequence how polytopes are initialized makes a difference when checking for isequal. ``Segment((1,0), (0,0)) == Segment((0,0), (1,0))`` returns ``false`` This is due to the implementaion in ``polytopes.jl`` in line 60: ``==(p1::Polytope, p2::Polytope) = vertices(p1) == vertices(p2)`` I see that the sequence of points is important but any cyclic permutation should be allowed. For Segments a solution could be: ``==(s1::Segments, s2::Segments) = Set(vertices(s1)) == Set(vertices(s2))`` Maybe there is a solution to check for all cyclic permutations for polytopes in general
