Pull request opened by KameronKeller: Add auth. This PR adds: - Middleware for authentication and authorization. Once we have the db setup, we can come back and finish the `authenticate` function so that it gets the role for a user from the database - It also adds bcrypt, jsonwebtoken, and eslint packages To test this code: 1. `npm install` 2. Paste the following into `api/users.js` ```js const { Router } = require("express"); const { authenticate, authorize, ROLES } = require("../lib/auth"); const router = Router(); router.get( "/", authenticate, // This list defines which roles are allowed access to this endpoint authorize([ROLES.admin, ROLES.instructor]), (req, res) => { res.status(200).send("Hello Users"); } ); module.exports = router; ``` 3. Manually generate a JWT on the command line (start a node REPL): ``` node ``` Paste the following into the REPL and copy the returned JWT ```js const jwt = require("jsonwebtoken"); const SECRET_KEY = "random-secret-key-P7YlYdCRJOiE9LUt4GjqrNnhVfrWDcwi"; jwt.sign({ sub: 'fakeId' }, SECRET_KEY, { expiresIn: "24h" }); ``` 4. Start the server: ``` npm start ``` 5. Paste the generated JWT into a curl command ``` curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " http://localhost:3000/users ```

type_text: Issue opened by snipercup: Still lines in terrain between chunks. Tried to fix the lines in #156 and it works for the most part, but there are still lines showing up between chunks. This is a tricky one because you could eliminate all faces at the edge of a chunk, but then you need to assume that wherever the chunk is placed, all blocks on all edges will be set against another block in another chunk. In a perfect solution you would know what is on every side of a block, even if the other blocks are not on the same chunk. It should be possible, because when a chunk is instanced, the levelgenerator already has the name and rotation of the neighbor chunk. It will be more difficult with random generation within chunks though.

Issue opened by snipercup: RockyHill: Containers on top of the hill are duplicated. When re-entering the RockyHill map and climbing to the top, the container that was created after you destroy the furniture has duplicated Steps to reproduce: - Start a new game - Travel to RockyHill using the overmap - Climb to the top and destroy the chair from a distance - Observe there is one container - Travel back to 0,0 using the overmap - Travel back to the same rockyhill as you were before and climb to the top - Observe there are now two containers This is probably cause by the container being close to the edge of the chunks and two of them consider the container to be part of it. So when the chunks are re-loaded, they both spawn the same container, duplicating them.

Issue opened by snipercup: Implement reading/writing of player skills. The player has skills, but isn't using them at the moment. Change the skill variable definition - Right now it's just a dictionary with a skill name and a level number. We need to change it so that in addition to the level number, we also define the amount of XP in that skill Add methods for reading skills - Get the current level of a skill - Get the current amount of xp for a skill Add methods for writing skills - Set the level of a skill - Set the amount of xp for a skill - Add an amount of levels to a skill, increasing the skill level - Add an amount of xp to a skill, increasing the skill xp. This should also include increasing the skill level when the xp reaches 100 Optional: - Add signals that emit when a skill level changes so that the characterwindow will update and maybe the recipes in the recipewindow will refresh. - Edit the character window to show the amount of xp for that skill, possibly with some visual to indicate how close it is to a level increase Down the line: - Work out some formula to balance skill increase and define recipe complexity. You don't want to get to level 100 crafting lockpicks. There should be some kind of deminishing return

Issue opened by snipercup: Implement basic crafting skills into recipes/crafting menu. Requires #191 We have skills defined but they aren't used yet. Here is my implementation idea: Edit the ItemCraftEditor and add: - The skill requirement, which is made up of a skill name and a number - The skill progression which is made up of a skill name and an amount of XP - The controls should allow the user to drag a skill from the skill list in the contenteditor and drop it on the skill name control Edit Gamedata to have the skill reference the recipe - Add an on_recipe_changed function that will add itself as a reference to the skill that has been configured for this recipe - Add an on_recipe_deleted function that will remove it's reference from the skill - Add an on_skill_deleted function that will remove itself from a recipe if it is deleted Edit the crafting menu: - Hide the recipe if the skill requirement is not met (assuming every recipe is autolearn for now) - Show the skill name and the amount of xp you will get by crafting the item - When the item is crafted, add the amount of xp to the player's skill

I am looking at Gamedata but I can't see an on_recipe_deleted function that will delete itself from item references if it is deleted - Modify remove_references_of_deleted_id and add the deleted recipe - The on_recipe_deleted can be like on_mob_deleted except the map update part This will help our references stay accurate

Issue opened by snipercup: Implement basic ranged skills into ranged combat. Requires #191 We have ranged skills but aren't using them yet. This idea describes a basic implementation idea Edit the ItemRangedEditor and add: - The skill progression which is made up of a skill name and an amount of XP when using the weapon - The controls should allow the user to drag a skill from the skill list in the contenteditor and drop it on the skill name control Edit Gamedata to have the skill reference the recipe - Modify the on_item_changed function so that it will add itself as a reference to the skill that has been configured for this item - Modify the on_item_deleted function that will remove it's reference from the skill - Add/update an on_skill_deleted function that will remove itself from an item if it is deleted Edit the EquippedItem: - Modify the accuracy calculations to use the skill of the gun that is equipped. This means adjusting the direction in perform_ranged_attack based on the skill of the player. We can say that the player needs level 30 to fire 100% accurate and starts with a minimum accuracy of 25%. This can be represented by a cone of accuracy that gets smaller when it reaches 100%. - Modify the perform_ranged_attack function to add the xp configured in the weapon to the skill so the player levels up.

Issue opened by snipercup: Implement athletics skill into sprinting. Requires #191 We have an athletics skill, but it doesn't do anything yet. Here is my idea of using it while running Edit player.gd: - Modify the _physics_process function to use the athletics skill. - Let's say that the starts with a minimum run_multiplier of 1.1. At level 50 it will be the normal run_multiplier of 1.5 and at level 100 the run_multiplier will be 2. We can fiddle with the numbers later - Let's say that at level 0 the stamina_lost_while_running_persec is 15. At level 50 it will be the normal 10 and at level 100 it will be 5 - Let's do the reverse with stamina_regen_while_standing_still where it starts at about 3, then increases to 6 at level 50 and increases to 8 at level 100 - Add the xp of running to the athletics skill so the player can level up

Issue opened by snipercup: Implement basic melee skills into melee combat. Requires #191 We have ranged skills but aren't using them yet. This idea describes a basic implementation idea Edit the ItemMeleeEditor and add: - The skill progression which is made up of a skill name and an amount of XP when using the weapon - The controls should allow the user to drag a skill from the skill list in the contenteditor and drop it on the skill name control Edit Gamedata to have the skill reference the recipe - Modify the on_item_changed function so that it will add itself as a reference to the skill that has been configured for this item - Modify the on_item_deleted function that will remove it's reference from the skill - Add/update an on_skill_deleted function that will remove itself from an item if it is deleted Edit the EquippedItem: - Add a hit chance that improves when the skill is higher. Let's say that the player has a 100% hit chance from level 80 and 25% hit chance at level 1 - Use the attack_cooldown_timer to control the swing speed. At level 0 it should be 1.5 seconds. At level 50 it should be 1 second. At level 100 it should be 0.5 seconds - Modify the perform_melee_attack function to add the xp configured in the weapon to the skill so the player levels up. Down the line we can implement swing speed per weapon or weapon class. We can also implement critical hits and maybe weaknesses.

Issue closed by snipercup: Still lines in terrain between chunks. Tried to fix the lines in #156 and it works for the most part, but there are still lines showing up between chunks. This is a tricky one because you could eliminate all faces at the edge of a chunk, but then you need to assume that wherever the chunk is placed, all blocks on all edges will be set against another block in another chunk. In a perfect solution you would know what is on every side of a block, even if the other blocks are not on the same chunk. It should be possible, because when a chunk is instanced, the levelgenerator already has the name and rotation of the neighbor chunk. It will be more difficult with random generation within chunks though.

Issue closed by bruno-at-orange: Wrong driver list in the status info. The status flag of Khiops displays usefull informations in stdout ```bash MODL_openmpi -s Khiops 10.2.2-b.1 Driver 'GCS driver' for URI scheme 'gs' System resources : Host number 1 Physical cores on system 8 Logical processes on system 1 Available memory on system 31.1 GB (Logical 19.4 GB) Available disk space on system 721.0 GB hostname MPI ranks logical memory disk cores yd-f5dt4d3 0 19.4 GB 721.0 GB 8 System PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS" NAME="Ubuntu" VERSION_ID="22.04" system=Linux release=6.5.0-35-generic version=#35~22.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue May 7 09:00:52 UTC 2 ``` Here we can see that the gcs driver is loaded. When the file server is activated, the gcs driver is not displayed anymore, It is replaced by the internal (and technical) "remote" driver: ```bash MODL_openmpi -s Khiops 10.2.2-b.1 Driver 'Remote driver' for URI scheme 'file' ``` We should have only the gcs driver, the file driver is hidden to the users. Questions: should we display only external driver as it is planned or should we display all drivers ? The second option is simpler and perhaps useful ...

Issue opened by marcboulle: Feedback from beta-test. ### Description Retour de béta-test, en vrac, pour discussion #### Menu "Help/Quick start": "Fast path" vs "Normal path" - Renommer "Normal path" en "Standard path"? #### En mode "Fast path", voir le Dictionary" en évidence est génant (premier menu, premiers champs de la fenêtre "Train database") - il s'agit d'un conflit d'ergonomie - mode fast path: on voudrait "invisibiliser" les dictionnaires - mode standard: le dictionnaire (notamment en multi-table) est un choix préalable, qui conditionne la structure de la liste des "data table files" - compromis actuel acceptable? - mode standard - mode privilégié, car il représente l'essentiel des usages au quotidien - mode fast path - permet de faire des démos/formations en quelques clics - utile également même en mode expert, pour la découverte de nouvelles données - mais nécessite une micro-formation - cf. info-bulle sur le champ "Analysis dictionary" du panneau "Train database" - cf. menu "Help/Quick start" #### Ajout d'un menu dans la fenêtre "Manage dictionaries"? Non fluidité de l'ergonomie: - quand on construit un dictionnaire en mode "fast path", on peut ensuite l'affiner dans le fenêtre "Dictionary management", mais on ne peut le sauver que depuis le menu "Data dictionary" de la fenêtre principale - suggestion: rajouter le menu "Data dictionary" de la fenêtre principale dans la fenêtre "Dictionary management"? - pro: cela rend la sous-fenêtre "Dictionary management" complétement autonome - cons: menus redondants ### Context - Khiops version: 10.5.0-b.1

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: Script de estructura. Tomando como referencia el diagrama del punto anterior, tienen que escribir las sentencias de SQL que crearán las tablas y sus relaciones. ● Deberá incluir la creación de la base de datos (create database…). ● Deberá incluir la creación de todas las tablas del sitio (create table…). ● Deberá incluir los tipos de datos de los campos y sus restricciones (primary keys, (not) null, unique, default, etc). ● Deberá incluir las relaciones entre las diferentes tablas (foreign keys). Entregable: archivo structure.sql que permita crear la base de datos completa.

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: (Opcional) Script de datos. El script de datos permite que cualquier desarrollador descargue el proyecto, ejecute el script y ya pueda ver el sitio funcionado sin más pasos. El script debería: ● Poblar la tabla de usuarios. ● Poblar la tabla de productos. ● Poblar las tablas secundarias (categorías, marcas, colores, talles, etc). ● (Opcional) Poblar la tabla de carrito de compras. ● (Opcional) Poblar la tabla de productos de carritos de compras. Una vez definidos los campos de sus tablas, nuevamente pueden utilizar Mockaroo, pero esta vez para generar el archivo SQL con datos. Entregable: archivo con extensión data.sql que permita poblar la base con datos.

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: Creación de carpeta Sequelize y archivos de modelos. Mediante la herramienta sequelize-cli deberán crear la carpeta que contenga los archivos de configuración de Sequelize. Una vez configurado Sequelize, seguirá crear los archivos de modelos para explicarle cómo es la estructura de la base de datos. La carpeta database deberá incluir: ● Los archivos de configuración para que Sequelize se conecte a la base de datos. ● Los archivos de modelos para representar las tablas de: ○ Usuarios. ○ Productos. ○ Tablas secundarias (categorías, marcas, colores, talles, etc). ○ (Opcional) Carrito de compras. ○ (Opcional) Productos de cada carrito de compras. ● Los modelos deben incluir todas las relaciones existentes en la base de datos. Entregable: carpeta database que incluya los archivos de configuración y archivos de modelos junto con sus relaciones.

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: Validaciones del front-end. Ya lo dijimos muchas veces y vale repetir: si bien no podemos confiar en las validaciones del front-end porque nuestro visitante puede deshabilitarlas, en el 99% de los casos funcionarán como esperamos. Nuestro objetivo acá es doble: 1. Por un lado, vamos a validar los datos antes de enviarlos para evitarle procesos innecesarios al servidor. 2. Por el otro, vamos a darle feedback inmediato y de calidad a nuestro visitante. Esto se traduce en una mucho mejor experiencia (UX) dentro de nuestro sitio. ● Registro de usuarios ○ Nombre y apellido ■ Obligatorio. ■ Deberá tener al menos 2 caracteres. ○ Email ■ Obligatorio. ■ Deberá ser válido. ■ (Opcional) → No puede repetirse con los e-mails ya registrados. ○ Contraseña ■ Obligatoria. ■ Deberá tener al menos 8 caracteres. ■ (Opcional) → Deberá tener letras mayúsculas, minúsculas, un número y un carácter especial. ○ Imagen ■ Deberá ser un archivo válido (JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF). ● Creación y modificación de productos ○ Nombre ■ Obligatorio. ■ Deberá tener al menos 5 caracteres. ○ Descripción ■ Deberá tener al menos 20 caracteres. ○ Imagen ■ Deberá ser un archivo válido (JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF).

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: Validaciones del backend. Si queremos hacer que nuestro sitio sea una fortaleza a prueba de corrupción de datos, necesitamos validar todos aquellos puntos donde nos llegue información desde el lado del usuario. Como ya se habrán imaginado, estamos hablando de los formularios. 📝🤓👌 Los siguientes puntos son una guía, su sitio puede requerir otras validaciones así que ajústense según lo necesiten. Issue closed by LeoVCruz: Dashboard en React. Ya tenemos nuestra fuente de datos y ahora solo queda consumirlas para darle vida a nuestro dashboard. Para este punto les recomendamos que partan de los archivos que les compartimos durante las ejercitaciones presenciales de React. El dashboard deberá contener al menos: ● 3 a 6 paneles simples con los siguientes totales: ○ Total de productos ○ Total de usuarios ○ Total de categorías ● Panel de detalle de último producto o usuario creado. ● Panel de categorías con el total de productos de cada una. ● Panel con el listado de productos.

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: Retrospectiva. Piensen qué hicieron bien el sprint anterior, qué hicieron mal, qué deberían empezar a hacer, qué deberían dejar de hacer, sigan esta dinámica. Ya estamos casi al final del viaje y, cuando terminen este sprint, les sugerimos que prueben la retrospectiva de línea de tiempo. A resumidas cuentas, esta consiste en dibujar una línea de tiempo que incluya todos los sprints y en ella ubicar post-its con cosas positivas (arriba de la línea) y negativas (debajo de la línea) que hayan ocurrido en cada etapa. Al terminar tendrán un resumen gráfico de todo el proceso.

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: API de productos Parte I. Nuestra API de productos será muy similar. Sus dos endpoints entregarán la lista completa de productos y el detalle de un producto en particular. Vamos con esas consignas: ● api/products/ ○ Deberá devolver un objeto literal con la siguiente estructura: ■ count → cantidad total de productos en la base. ■ countByCategory → objeto literal con una propiedad por categoría con el total de productos. ■ products → array con la colección de productos, cada uno con: ● id ● name ● description ● un array con principal relación de uno a muchos (ej: categories). ● detail → URL para obtener el detalle. Entregable: URL funcionales devolviendo datos de productos en formato JSON.

Issue closed by LeoVCruz: API de usuarios Parte II. Nuestra API de usuarios va a proveernos de dos endpoints muy importantes. El primero nos entregará la lista completa de usuarios y el segundo nos permitirá consultar los detalles de un usuario en particular. Vamos con esas consignas: ● api/users/:id ○ Deberá devolver un objeto literal con la siguiente estructura: ■ Una propiedad por cada campo en base. ■ Una URL para la imagen de perfil (para mostrar la imagen). ■ Sin información sensible (ej: password y categoría). ● api/users/:id ○ Deberá devolver un objeto literal con la siguiente estructura: ■ Una propiedad por cada campo en base. ■ Una URL para la imagen de perfil (para mostrar la imagen). ■ Sin información sensible (ej: password y categoría). Entregable: URL funcionales devolviendo datos de usuarios en formato JSON.

PR changes requested by CommonClimate: Global coherence. Nice work! A few minor changes to take it to 11. 1. On the code side, since `Series.global_coherence()` is built on top of wavelet_coherence(), I recommend having an optional parameter called `coh`, which would `None` by default, but would allow you to pass a coherence object from which the average would be taken. 2. The gcoh.plot() command should have a label on the right-hand side that says "coherence" (or "global coherence") by default, which could be controlled by a parameter called `ylabel_rhs` (similarly, need a `ylabel_lhs = PSD` by default) 3. On the docstring side, I recommend that the docstring for `Series.global_coherence()` does something with `gcoh` (e.g. plot it). Otherwise, it's a very frustrating docstring to read because it ends in a blind corner.

Issue opened by CommonClimate: EnsembleSeries __repr__ method. It's currently very difficult to peruse the contents of an `EnsembleSeries` object, and it doesn't need to be. Currently, the `__repr__` method (inherited from `MultipleSeries`) yields this when printing in a Jupyter Notebook: this is wrong, as this particular ensemble includes 1,000 members. Pull request merged by benitsch: #376: Wrong time slot for interventions in study timeline calendar.. Fixed the issue where interventions are shown in a different time slot in the Study Timeline calendar. * Later on in the code we use Transformers.toOffsetDateTime function, where the "Europe/Vienna" timezone is hardcoded, but we need to consider this timezone in the cronExpression as well, when we calculate the interventions. * If "Europe/Vienna" is not defined for the cronExpression, it will take the server timezone (which appears to be different), therefore the interventions were at a different time slot in the study timeline calendar. Reference: https://github.com/MORE-Platform/more-studymanager-frontend/issues/376

Pull request opened by vjousse: Run prettier and pre-commit hooks only on staged files. ## :wrench: Problem Currently, the pre-commit hook managed by husky run prettier on all the files for each commit, even if the files were not changed. It slows down the dev process unnecessarily most of the time. ## :cake: Solution Run linting only on staged files when commiting. ## :rotating_light: Points to watch / comments My first attempt was to keep using husky with https://github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged. It works well for prettier but doesn't work for ruff as it doesn't manage `pipenv run` nor `virtualenv` correctly. It looks very "javascript centric". My second and final attempt was to use https://pre-commit.com/. It's written in Python, it can manage every language (with hooks or using shell commands) and is well suited for our environment as we already use `pipenv` and Python. `npm` commands removed: - `format:check` => replaced by `lint:all` and changed in the CI file `npm` commands added: - `lint:prettier` lint one file using prettier. Used by other npm commands. - `lint:prettier:all` lint all files in the project using prettier. - `lint:ruff:all` lint all python files using ruff check and format (with sort option selected). - `lint:all` prettier and ruff lint on all files. - `fix:prettier` lint and fix the errors using prettier for one file (used in pre-commit hook) - `fix:prettier:all` lint and fix the errors using prettier for all the files. - `fix:ruff:all` lint all python files using ruff check and format (with sort option selected) and fix the errors - `fix:all` prettier and ruff fix on all files A `pyproject.toml` file was added to tell ruff to not check the `data/` directory. I've added some simple checks with pre-commit like yaml format, line-ending checks (avoid mixing windows/linux/macox line ending), trailing-spaces removal and a check to prevent commiting directly on master (I suppose the git repo is already configured to avoid that, but I like to have it locally before I push). ## :desert_island: How to test First, uninstall husky: npx husky uninstall Check that the command `git config --get core.hookspath` returns nothing. If it gives you something like `.husky/\_` unset it manually using `git config --unset-all core.hooksPath` Install pre-commit: pipenv install pipenv run pre-commit install Test that it's working as expected by issuing the following command: pipenv run pre-commit run --all-files You should get something like that: image

Pull request merged by vjousse: Run prettier and pre-commit hooks only on staged files. ## :wrench: Problem Currently, the pre-commit hook managed by husky run prettier on all the files for each commit, even if the files were not changed. It slows down the dev process unnecessarily most of the time. ## :cake: Solution Run linting only on staged files when commiting. ## :rotating_light: Points to watch / comments My first attempt was to keep using husky with https://github.com/lint-staged/lint-staged. It works well for prettier but doesn't work for ruff as it doesn't manage `pipenv run` nor `virtualenv` correctly. It looks very "javascript centric". My second and final attempt was to use https://pre-commit.com/. It's written in Python, it can manage every language (with hooks or using shell commands) and is well suited for our environment as we already use `pipenv` and Python. `npm` commands removed: - `format:check` => replaced by `lint:all` and changed in the CI file `npm` commands added: - `lint:prettier` lint one file using prettier. Used by other npm commands. - `lint:prettier:all` lint all files in the project using prettier. - `lint:ruff:all` lint all python files using ruff check and format (with sort option selected). - `lint:all` prettier and ruff lint on all files. - `fix:prettier` lint and fix the errors using prettier for one file (used in pre-commit hook) - `fix:prettier:all` lint and fix the errors using prettier for all the files. - `fix:ruff:all` lint all python files using ruff check and format (with sort option selected) and fix the errors - `fix:all` prettier and ruff fix on all files A `pyproject.toml` file was added to tell ruff to not check the `data/` directory. I've added some simple checks with pre-commit like yaml format, line-ending checks (avoid mixing windows/linux/macox line ending), trailing-spaces removal and a check to prevent commiting directly on master (I suppose the git repo is already configured to avoid that, but I like to have it locally before I push). ## :desert_island: How to test First, uninstall husky: npx husky uninstall Check that the command `git config --get core.hookspath` returns nothing. If it gives you something like `.husky/\_` unset it manually using `git config --unset-all core.hooksPath` Install pre-commit: pipenv install pipenv run pre-commit install Test that it's working as expected by issuing the following command: pipenv run pre-commit run --all-files You should get something like that: image

Pull request opened by vjousse: Use same ruff command on CI and in pre-commit. ## :wrench: Problem Currently we have different linting rules for ruff in the CI and in the pre-commit hook (we use `--extended-select I` in the CI/package.json and we don't in the pre-commit, error on my side). We use a dedicated `pre-commit` hook to fix/lint the python code when committing, but on the CI we use our usual `npm lint:all` script to check that everything is ok. If we modify our linting in `package.json`, it will not be reflected on the pre-commit hook and vice-versa. ## :cake: Solution Use `npm fix` commands in the pre-commit hook to be consistent with the CI. ## :rotating_light: Points to watch / comments I've added the `--force-exclude` to the ruff params so that it excludes files that are mentioned in `pyproject.toml` (it's not the default behavior when a filename is specified as a parameter and that's what pre-commit does) The `format` and `check` commands for ruff are a little bit weird. `format` require a `--check` flag to not write changes to files, and `check` requires the opposite (`--fix`) to write changes to files. At some point they will be unified (see https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/8232) but it's not the case yet. ## :desert_island: How to test `npm lint:all` and `npm fix:all` should work as usual.

Issue closed by ChristianHuehn: Progressbar breaks when it can't fit in one line. # Bug ## Expected Behavior WHEN Using a parser that implements the progresstracker THEN The progresstracker always correctly displays its progress in one self-updating line ## Actual Behavior When the commandline is too small, so part of the tracker gets put into a new line or other printlns happen during execution, it doesn't update the one line but prints a new one ## Screenshots image ## Steps to Reproduce the Problem 1. Make the commandline where you execute the ccsh small 2. Execute a parser that implements the progresstracker (e.g. RawTextParser) ## Specifications - CodeCharta Version: 1.120.1 - OS: Mac OS
Comment on issue by ChristianHuehn: Good finding, but not relevant enough to be planed in the near or far future.

Issue closed by ChristianHuehn: Inconsistent naming of parsers. # Bug ## Expected Behavior WHEN I open the interactive shell `ccsh -i` THEN I, as a user, want to see all parsers follow the same naming conventions. Optionally, id also like them sorted either by their type (import, filter, export, ...) or alphabetically ## Actual Behaviour Not all parsers follow the same naming convention (e.g. `edgefilter` contains the ending filter but `merge` does not) ## Screenshots ## Specifications - CodeCharta Version: 1.119.1

Issue closed by ChristianHuehn: PRs based on branches in repository forks do not run GH-Actions. # Bug: PRs based on branches in repository forks do not run GH-Actions ## Expected Behavior GIVEN A branch from someone who want to participate in this repository WHEN opening a PR on said branch (on a fork) THEN the applicable GH-actions like test.yml asks for a maintainer to be started or start themselves if possible. ## Actual Behavior They don't start and are forever stuck in _"Waiting for status to be reported"_, ## Steps to Reproduce the Problem 1. Create fork 1. Create branch 1. Open PR ## Specifications It must be checked whether this behavior is still occurring.

Issue closed by ChristianHuehn: Decouple CodeCharta from fixed metrics like MCC. # Feature request Resulted from https://github.com/MaibornWolff/codecharta/issues/3456 ## Description Some complexity metrics (e.g. from sonar) are imported and renamed into `mcc`, so that CodeCharta does know the most important complexity metric. But... **As** a User, **I want** to preserve the source metrics names and definition, **so that** I can use exactly these metrics in CodeCharta. At the moment, some metrics are mapped during import on custom acronyms that nobody can understand. We need to put further thoughts into this on how to get rid of the fixed core metrics in CodeCharta. ## Acceptance criteria - - - ## Assumptions & Exclusions ## Development notes (optional Task Breakdown) - [ ] There are hard references to `mcc`, `rloc` and maybe others in the code - [ ] - [ ] ## Open questions - How to be able to identify the main complexity metric, that is available from the cc.json file, so that features like Suspicious Metrics can work with it.

It would be super cool if the CSVImporter could also read this information out of the csv. ## Description As a developer, I want to specify edges in csv so that I can import them easily. ## Acceptance criteria - Given a csv with header "path, to_path" i want to create a cc.json with all path and to_path nodes and edges corresponding to the csv.

Issue closed by ChristianHuehn: Remove redundant dependencies in analysis. # Feature request ## Description As a developer, I want fewer dependencies in my projects so that redundant functionality is removed and attack surface is minimized. For example, we have a lot of dependencies/libraries for handling json files and content, maybe we can switch to one single library and use all of its functionality. ## Acceptance criteria - - - ## Assumptions & Exclusions In our Weekly on the 13th of September 2022 we decided that this should be an ongoing task, rather than one "big" issue. ## Development notes (optional Task Breakdown) - [ ] Check if we need Wiremock and if yes, switch to the new https://github.com/wiremock/wiremock repository - [x] Switch from Spek and JUnit4 to JUnit 5 #3202 - [ ] Decide on one assertion plugin ( jsonassert and assertJ, ... ) are currently in use) - [ ] Decide on one JSON plugin (JSON, GSON, Jackson and jsonassert are currently in use) - [ ] Unify/Verify which mockking library we use (io.mockk // mockito-core // com.nhaarman.mockitokotlin etc.) - [ ] Update ADR to write down these decisions for future reference ## Open questions

Issue closed by ChristianHuehn: Import CKJM Metrics. # Feature Request We want to import metrics generated by ckjm. This tools processes Java Bytecode and calculates for each class the following six metrics proposed by Chidamber and Kemerer. WMC: Weighted methods per class DIT: Depth of Inheritance Tree NOC: Number of Children CBO: Coupling between object classes RFC: Response for a Class LCOM: Lack of cohesion in methods In addition it also calculates for each class Ca: Afferent couplings NPM: Number of public methods

description: GitHub repository MindscapeHQ/raygun4node: Node.JS SDK for Raygun (JavaScript, 30 stars) Event window: June 01 - 07, 2024.
type_text: Issue opened by paul-uz: Multiple errors sent, only one received. I am sending multiple errors in a test function on AWS Lambda and I am using the new `await` version of `send()` with batches disabled in the client. I only see one error in raygun after running the function.
Comment on issue by miquelbeltran: Hi @paul-uz are the error instances grouped in Raygun?

Comment on issue by paul-uz: > Hi @paul-uz are the error instances grouped in Raygun? No they weren't. I've tried to change to message based grouping and I think that helped a bit. How up to date is the node hasher? It's on version 1 and the node package only just got an update in 2 years so maybe it needs some attention?

Comment on issue by miquelbeltran: Is there a change you can set the environment variable `DEBUG` to `raygun` and send us a log? The log should contain the lines `[raygun.ts] Successfully sent message ...` each time an error is sent using the `send()` method. I need to check why the Raygun API is grouping errors even when the `error.message` is different.
Comment on issue by miquelbeltran: Can you also provide some sample code showing how you use the raygun client?

Comment on issue by mo-nathan: When looking to populate the form fields I've been looking at the usage of notes templates for existing observations. There is a fair amount of usage (1000s of observations) and it's is common for there to be data that corresponds to data for the field slip forms. There are currently 126 distinct note template fields. The relevant ones for the field slip data relate to who the collector was (2552 cases), what the name/id was (2445 - dominated by the Ceskas), and who the identifier was (655). In all three cases there is more than one field name used and in many cases the field name is used by more than one user: ``` Collector: :Collector or :collector, 560 cases, 5 users :Collector's_Name or :Collector's_name, 1289 cases, 19 users :Collector(s), 703 cases, 3 users ID_By: :Identifier, 354, 4 users :Identified_by, 301, 1 user (Ceskas) ID: :Preliminary_Identification, 452, 1 user (Joe) :Original_ID, 257, 1 user (Ceskas) :Original_Herbarium_Label, 1599, 1 user (Ceskas) :Accepted_ID, 8, 1 user (Ceskas) :"Accepted_ID/Name", 129, 1 user (Ceskas) ``` Note that case sort matters in the code, but the MySQL LIKE matcher ignores case. I don't think there is any reason to actually treat case differences differently so I've lumped them together above. So the core question is how should this data be used relative to the field slip data. It seems reasonable if someone is applying a field slip to an existing observation to look for matches that seem to be carrying to relevant data. The big question is what to do if the user saves field slip data with changes. Should the existing field get overwritten? For observations without this data we need field names. My initial thought was "ID", "ID_By", and "Collector". However, given that "Collector" is already in use, maybe the field slip fields should have a distinct prefix (e.g., "Field_Slip_ID", "Field_Slip_ID_By", and "Field_Slip_Collector")?

I like the idea of condensing "Collector's Name" in to "Collector" and generally forcing convention over configuration when useful.

Pull request opened by benthecarman: Fixes for olympus swaps. Previously when doing a swap we'd get an extra channel sometimes because we'd call the fee api multiple time which would cause the olympus node to open the extra channel. To make sure we only call the fee api once, we need to generate the invoice when estimating fee and then when we execute the swap, use that invoice, this way we can guarantee there is only a single call to the api for a given swap.

Pull request opened by benthecarman: Claim zaps in batches. Helps with #1163 Before we'd claim each zap individually and this could cause problems because relays would send the events with the newest first, so if we stopped claiming the zaps for whatever reason (user closes app), then we'd miss the remaining zaps because we'd set our sync timestamp to the first one we claimed. This fixes this problem by instead accumulating all the zaps until we get the End Of Stored Events message from the relays, and then claiming the zaps, this way we know we got everything from the relay.

Comment on issue by Neriderc: I think I've fixed this. I worked out how to disable "pretty URLs" as I believe you both have servers with this disabled, and I saw the issue that you are having. I thought I had accounted for this, but it seems the URL often shows the HTML code '%2F' instead of the character it stands for ('/'), and so I have updated the check to correct this before testing the URL. I'm using the URL for a couple of things, but the important part here I think is the check for whether it is an individual. It looks for '/individual/' in the URL (which I believe is always in English, based on a quick glance at the webtrees source code). If this is not found, it is treated as a family record and the default action applies (if URLs are enabled, it would open the link). This problem would not result in an error in the browser log, as no error would be encountered. I have made this change in the main branch and tested that it works for me. If you could update from the main branch again and test it, that would be great!

Comment on issue by schuco: After working with the change resulting in a fixed zoom level for some months now (since November 2023), it is my experience, that this change has not been favourable in all cases. Especially when I am displaying a big tree the strong zoom on the last individual added opens a much too narrow scope of the tree. In most cases it is my first action to widen the zoom before I can inspect the result of adding the last individual. The present approach may be more useful in a top-to-bottom diagram than in left-to-right diagram, which I am maily applying. **Proposal:** When a fixed zoom is used the scope should include at least the parent generation and the direct offspring generation. Maybe a dynamic solution could be useful, where the zoom diaplay a preset proportion of the tree.

Review comment on PR by sanjayankur31: I was thinking about this yesterday. Instead of re-defining these classes, can we not just use the classes already defined in libNeuroML? - `neuroml.Morphology` -> can be the "top level morphology object" either as is, or extended to `MorphologySWC` or something if it needs tweaking? - `neuroml.Segment` - `neuroml.SegmentGroup` - `neuroml.Point3DWithDiam` Finally, if we use `neuroml.Cell` as the overall object, you get to use all the helper functions to add segments/segment groups, optimise the morphology and the graph representation related functions of the morphology that we've implemented for `neuroml.Cell` too. For example, if we simply collect all the segments and make sure they pass the basic tests (which could be added to the neuroml.Cell class), we could maybe just even use the `create_unbranched_segment_groups` helper function to automatically create the first iteration unbranched segment groups: https://libneuroml.readthedocs.io/en/latest/userdocs/coreclasses.html#neuroml.nml.nml.Cell.create_unbranched_segment_group_branches So, what's the advantage of redefining them vs just reusing them? What do you think?

Review comment on PR by sanjayankur31: this is good for a start, but there are going to be a lot of more segment groups in the cell. Each unbranched section of the morphology is a segment group. All of these will be of one of the standard types: soma or dendrite or axon. So, we also need to detect all the SWC sections that form an unbranched chain and put those in a segment group. See the `add_unbranched_segment_group` helper function in the neuroml.Cell class: https://libneuroml.readthedocs.io/en/latest/userdocs/coreclasses.html#neuroml.nml.nml.Cell.add_unbranched_segment_group also: https://libneuroml.readthedocs.io/en/latest/userdocs/coreclasses.html#neuroml.nml.nml.Cell.add_unbranched_segments

Review comment on PR by sanjayankur31: Please disregard this bit for the moment. Let's start with a representation that is completely independent of NeuroML---this way this will be a general (NeuroML independent) API for working with SWC that other tools can also use. So, instead, the way to go would be to create a data structure---a tree/graph where each node corresponds to a line in the swc storing the information there: co-ordinates/diameter/parent/type etc. Once we have this, we can query it to ask "what are the parents of this node", or "what are all the nodes of type X that have more than one parent" etc. For neuroml.Cell, I'd created a networkx representation of the points, and then that allows us to use the networkx API to loop over the graph and query it etc. Take a look at the following functions in nml.py in the development branch of libneuroml: - `get_adjacency_list` - `get_graph` - `create_unbranched_segment_groups` - `get_morphology_root` they use

Review comment on PR by sanjayankur31: I wonder if we can move this functionality into the `plot_3D_cell_morphology` function, and add an argument there to activate this transformation (instead of passing `x_angle` and `y_angle` pass: `pcaify=True` (with a better argument name, of course :))? I wonder because this is limited to the case where we're plotting a single cell, so it sort of fits better there. One should also be able to use this when using `plot_3D_cell_morphology` directly? It'll also mean that the rotation + translation only happens once. At the moment, in the hay model, for example, it's happening multiple times---each time the mesh precision is dropped.

Review comment on PR by sanjayankur31: I assume the order of operations is important---would it be different if we: - first translated the cell to origin - did the pca - rotated the cell about the soma (origin)?

Review comment on PR by lej0hn: Yes this is the goal, this just allowed for visualization of the pca axes for debugging. However, besides not being able to visualize the pca axes after this change, I think there is another issue with the camera, as you noted above. So, the bounding box that's used to center the camera is taken in `plot _interactive_3d` , before the cell is translated to origin or rotated, so the bounding box and therefore the camera, is centered on the original cell's position. Since in this case we're translating the cell to the origin, maybe along with `pcaify=True` , we could set an extra argument in `create_new_vispy_canvas` that sets the `view_center` of the camera at the origin as well?

Review comment on PR by lej0hn: - first translated the cell to origin - did the pca These two steps can be done in any order ,I believe, without any change because the PCA first translates the points so that their center is at the origin and then applies other computations. But after that, the best way is in fact to translate and then rotate, now that I think of it, because the rotations and the angles are calculated based on the PCA axis, which starts at the origin. So to apply them succesfully to the cell, it should be close to the origin in order to have similar results.

Review comment on PR by sanjayankur31: Yeh. So, if there's only one cell, we don't need to call `create_new_vispy_canvas` in `plot_3D_interactive` at all. I can't remember why I did it there. It doesn't seem necessary. We could conditionalise it there so that it's only called when there's more than one cell to be plotted, otherwise we let `plot_3D_cell_morphology` or `plot_3D_schematic` do it when it finds that `current_canvas` and `current_view` are `None`. I just remembered that we also have the `plot_3D_schematic` function too, where it'll also be good to apply the PCA method so that the schematic is also upright. So perhaps we need to split out the PCA bits into a new method that takes a cell as argument and returns the "upright" cell? This could be called by both `plot_3D_cell_morphology` and `plot_3D_schematic` before they create the canvas and the meshes etc? Yes, we could add another optional argument to `create_new_vispy_canvas` called `view_center`, which if provided will be used. If it isn't, we'll calculate the centre from `view_min` and `view_max`? How does that sound?

Review comment on PR by bertsky: I'm sorry, I should have read your statement more carefully. I thought you meant the _existing_ OcrdMetsServer API, not some new API merely calling its CLI (as you now implemented). IMO using `multiprocessing.Process` on the API instead of `subprocess.Popen` on the CLI is better because it is faster, needs no I/O or log handling and no killing – you can just yield to or stop the background thread.

Review comment on PR by MehmedGIT: The I/O in this case is used for logging the OcrdMetsServer logs to a file. I am not sure why you want to get rid of that. The class OcrdMetsServer is instantiated separately for every workspace. Do you mean a single OcrdMetsServer process but many threads for the different instantiations? I am a bit confused on that one.

Review comment on PR by bertsky: I did not mean actual threads, I am still referring to `multiprocessing.Process`. One background process per METS Server / workspace – but as `Process` object (API) instead of a `Popen` object (CLI). I thought the logs should go to the processing job log file as well. But I can now see it would take additional configuration to have the forked subprocess log to the corresponding process job log file. If you don't see benefits in avoiding additional CLI parsing, then let's leave it at that – it's a cosmetic point anyway.

Review comment on PR by MehmedGIT: > One background process per METS Server / workspace – but as Process object (API) instead of a Popen object (CLI). Yeah, but then we lose the separate logging per mets file, that's why I asked if you know a workaround for that. > I thought the logs should go to the processing job log file as well. Only OCR-D processor logs go inside the processing job logs. The mets server logs just logs the requests and responses for debugging purposes if needed. > If you don't see benefits in avoiding additional CLI parsing, then let's leave it at that – it's a cosmetic point anyway. I just do not see how the conversion could be done while keeping the separate mets server log files. The logging has caused some big issues in the past. The separation of logging is more straightforward with the current implementation. If it's just a cosmetic point, then I would just avoid making changes on that part and potentially mess the logging.

Comment on issue by bertsky: @kba you commented > Changes as of 2023-08-20: > > - Try to be less intrusive with OCR-D specific logging conventions to make it easier and less surprising to define logging behavior when using OCR-D/core as a library > - Change setOverrideLogLevel to only override the log level of the ``ocrd`` logger and its descendants > - initLogging will set exactly one handler, for the root logger or for the ``ocrd`` logger. > - Child loggers should propagate to the ancestor logging (default behavior of the logging library - no more PropagationShyLogger) > - disableLogging only removes any handlers from the ``ocrd`` logger But how did you intend to effect that all loggers (e.g. `processor.Tesserocr`) are inheriting from `ocrd`?

Issue opened by stweil: Missing / incomplete license statement. This repository uses the Apache License 2.0, but does not mention it in the README files. So this fact is only visible in pyproject.toml and indirectly because a LICENSE file exists. The Python code uses frozendict and paramiko, two Python modules which use the LGPL. I think this is allowed (although some people disagree), but the LGPL requires at least a bit of documentation: "Give prominent notice with each copy of the Combined Work that the Library is used in it and that the Library and its use are covered by this License." Therefore I think that we should add a license statement to the documentation which not only mentions the Apache License explicitly, but also the two Python modules and their use of the LGPL.

Comment on issue by bertsky: > It just didn't occur to me, I wanted to make the downloads reversible on the METS level but we can add the option to actually remove the files. Then for the sake of consistency I recommend doing the opposite: making the filesystem action the default and adding an option `-k, --keep-file Do not delete file from file system`.

Issue opened by bertsky: workspace prune-files: also removes remote FLocats. The documentation for the `prune-files` command says: > Removes mets:files that point to non-existing local files However, that's not what is implemented: https://github.com/OCR-D/core/blob/26a3f787cd7746b8e197427e74c532edbecefd8b/src/ocrd/cli/workspace.py#L560-L577 So either the documentation should read… > Removes mets:files that do not point to existing local files …or the implementation should not remove files that also have a `.url`. Since we also have `workspace find ... --undo-download` (removing `.local_filename` in METS and filesystem for those entries which also have a `.url` – if implemented properly, i.e. fixing #1150) the former makes more sense to me, as the latter would be redundant behaviour.

Comment on issue by bertsky: > > It just didn't occur to me, I wanted to make the downloads reversible on the METS level but we can add the option to actually remove the files. > > Then for the sake of consistency I recommend doing the opposite: making the filesystem action the default and adding an option `-k, --keep-file Do not delete file from file system`. Alternatively, we could implement a generic-purpose command `clean`, complementary to prune-files and undo-download: removing files in the workspace which are not referenced in the METS.

Comment on PR by joschrew: The problem is this: When the images are created the logfiles might be created as well. For example when a processor's image extends core and then calls ocrd core for loading resources. Then the logfiles are created. Then a user creates a container of this processor and the logs are root-owned which cause problems when the user of the container is not root. So I don't think a variable can really help here. This problem is avoidable though, with setting a separate logging-conf or with pre deleting the logfiles in the image before starting the container. This PR is like a quick fix for this problem. But other fixes are possible as well. So if we don't want this world permission logfiles it is not that big problem. Therefore my suggestion is to close and not merge this PR and go with something like https://github.com/OCR-D/ocrd_all/pull/429 and do the same in the processor-images which also have those logfiles created. We have to touch the images anyway when setting the core version. Sry for being late with this suggestion, I forgot to mention this issue in our last meetings.

Issue opened by mistryrn: Investigate and Fix Inconsistent Consent UI Production Build Runtime Errors (Possibile Next.js Barrel File Problem). Some builds of Consent UI exhibit an issue where a runtime `TypeError` occurs when calling functions imported from barrel file exports. For example, over the past few months there have been two builds that we know of (`7c48ac4e` is the latest) where Participant Registration fails due to: ```js TypeError: (0 , A.createRegisteredParticipant) is not a function ``` We suspect it may be related to the way Next.js handles imports from barrel files, as 1. Next.js has documented their approach to optimizing barrel imports: - https://vercel.com/blog/how-we-optimized-package-imports-in-next-js 2. This function (`createRegisteredParticipant`) is being imported from a nested barrel file export: - a. Import in question: https://github.com/OHCRN/platform/blob/7c48ac4e9881ff02b06e9c4c7beadc09434084b7/apps/consent-ui/src/components/views/Register/handleCreateRegisteredParticipant.tsx#L28 - b. Barrel export 1: https://github.com/OHCRN/platform/blob/7c48ac4e9881ff02b06e9c4c7beadc09434084b7/apps/consent-ui/src/services/api/requests/index.ts#L27 - c. Barrel export 2 (where it is being imported from in `a`): https://github.com/OHCRN/platform/blob/7c48ac4e9881ff02b06e9c4c7beadc09434084b7/apps/consent-ui/src/services/api/index.ts#L21 Unfortunately, this issue is very inconsistent. Most builds do not exhibit this issue, and it is often remedied by re-triggering the production build of Consent UI to generate and deploy a new docker image (without making any code changes). A permanent fix for this **might** be to simply remove the use of barrel files within the Consent UI package. However, there have been several discussions online regarding similar errors, some of which suggest simply upgrading Next.js as the solution. - https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/62953 - https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/63494 ## Exit Criteria - [ ] Complete an investigation into the issue - [ ] Implement a permanent fix, tested by running multiple local docker builds of consent-ui pointed at the DEV environment and checking for consistency

Issue opened by magnesj: Octave: Make it possible to build Octave plugins as a separate build job. The building of Octave plugins within main ResInsight build on `RHEL8` cause the build to use gcc-12. This version of gcc is extremely slow when building `opm-common`. Adjust the `CMake` configuration so it is possible to build the Octave plugins as a completely separate build job. These binaries can then be uploaded to an external server. The main ResInsight build can then download the binaries and include them in the install package.

type_text: Pull request opened by hepcat72: Gracefully handle stale maintained `Animal.last_serum_sample` maintained field. ## Summary Change Description Caught a situation where the `Animal.last_serum_sample` maintained field value can be invalid due to manual data manipulation and added an error status with a message suggesting that maintained fields be rebuilt. While I was at it, I addressed a TODO item in the same serum_validity code: > `TODO: MSRunSequence.date can no longer be null, so these warnings can probably be removed` An example of the exception previously encountered is in the issue's current behavior section. This is now what the user gets from this PR when the maintained field value is incorrect: stalemtf This is what caused the exception to occur: The `last_serum_sample` should be on dev, which is still what it is in my sandbox: ``` In [1]: from DataRepo.models import Animal In [2]: anml = Animal.objects.get(name="20220818M1") In [3]: anml._last_serum_sample() Out[3]: In [4]: anml.last_serum_sample Out[4]: ``` This is what it became on dev: ``` In [1]: from DataRepo.models import Animal In [2]: anml = Animal.objects.get(name="20220818M1") Adding propagation handler to Animal.studies.through In [3]: anml._last_serum_sample() Out[3]: In [4]: anml.last_serum_sample ``` I believe that manual database manipulations caused the value to become `None`. As you can see, the method that generates the value, still generates the correct value. It's just that the value saved got wiped out. Just calling: ``` In [4]: anml.save() ``` automatically fixes the maintained fields: mntfldfixd This PR doesn't fix the values, it just makes it fail gracefully and tell us what needs to be done to fix the problem (in the tooltip). Note, I should have started a screen session yesterday when I ran `rebuild_maintained_fields`, because my session went stale and the rebuild was rolled back. I'm going to take a quick look at the script. I think it has a surgical option to make it only apply to certain labeled autoupdate routes. I may also reintroduce the ability to suspend cache updates. I'd previously eliminated that to make it better encapsulated, but I can add it to the management command... ## Affected Issues/Pull Requests - Resolves #985 ## Review Notes See comments in-line. ## Checklist This pull request will be merged once the following requirements are met. The author and/or reviewers should uncheck any unmet requirements: - Review requirements - Minimum approvals: 1 - No changes requested - All blocking issues resolved by reviewers - Specific reviewers: @__add_username_here__ - Review period: 2 days - Associated issue/pull request requirements: - [x] All requirements in affected issues marked "resolved" are satisfied - [x] All required pull requests are merged *(or none)* - Basic requirements - [x] All linters pass - [x] All tests pass - [x] All conflicts resolved - Overhead requirements - [x] New/changed method tests implemented/updated *(or no change)* - [x] Updated *Unreleased* section of `changelog.md` *(or no change)* - [x] Migrations created & committed *(or no change)*

Comment on PR by hepcat72: Just as a side-note, I created a separate branch to run the rebuild without caching retrievals or updates and I ran it again, this time using the `--labels` option to only perform auto-updates of maintained fields with the `fcirc_calcs` label: ``` ``` ...and it too only 4 minutes. It updated all the other animals' values as well as fields in other models with the same label, totaling 6,137 field value updates. They appear to all have been rendered stale, looking at the console output. I then updated all fields and it updated 6,310 fields, still in about 4 minutes. I didn't realize that we only use 1 other label: "name" and it's just for the infusate updates, which explains why so few more fields were updated. So it seems that the cache suspension *REALLY* speeds up the `rebuild_maintained_fields` script. Plus, you don't get deluged with cache messages (aside from the ones for class registration). I'll be submitting a PR shortly.

Review comment on PR by hepcat72: `MaintainedModel` was generically developed. It will work on any Django project. The only custom aspect is possibly missing features that we didn't need. But, nothing prevents new features from being added in a way that supports all cases. The speed issue in the caching implementation is the same issue I put thought into for `MaintainedModel`, and that is deferred update decorators, so that fields are updated en-masse after all the changes are done. This is how the design choices in `MaintainedModel` can be implemented in `HierCachedModel`. `HierCachedModel` was initially designed to only support updates when the cache is stale during cached value retrieval. It wasn't implemented to interact well with loading. During a load, it ends up updating and re-updating the cache each time something in the hierarchy changes. `HierCachedModel` stands on top of the built-in django caching mechanism. It solves a problem with the builtin caching that causes pointless updates and occasionally stale/wrong values. It does this by mapping the relationships between models whose value changes should trigger a cache update. Thus, cache updates only ever happen when a change is necessary, and the values are never stale. Personally, I think the best path is the replace all cached fields with maintained fields.

Review comment on PR by hepcat72: So, I'll just point out that I know the convention. I'm very familiar. I learned quite a bit about how tracebacks are constructed when (and before) I implemented `AggregatedErrors`, so let me explain how it works. What I implemented allows you to handle exceptions and and still be able to continue processing **with a simulated traceback that doesn't exist in Python, when you continue processing**. These simulated tracebacks are not necessary. They're just a bonus. If this bonus print wasn't done, you would get (almost always) **nothing** in terms of a trace. Tracebacks are constructed item by item **as the code travels back through the call stack from the point where the exception was raised, to the place where it's caught**. Python provides no mechanism to get a traceback if you wish to catch and continue processing. You can print the exception message and you can get the partial traceback from the raise location and the catch, but that often time doesn't even include your own code, depending on where it's executed, which can be in an imported package. I was extracting these partial tracebacks in the exact way of the convention, but only when I was buffering the exception I caught. This new MO however, handles the case where the caught exception is repackaged as a different exception (in order to for example, provide context related to the input file). Everything I'm doing is to the convention of how this could be implemented in traditional Python code, except in traditional python code, if you catch an exception and continue processing, you only get a very short (often completely uninformative) traceback. So I implemented a way to approximate the traceback using `traceback.format_stack()`. That gets a formatted call stack from the very bottom to the current line of code where it's called. So instead of the stack being between the raise and catch, it's everything. I just filter out everything up to the last occurrence of `site-packages`. This creates more traceback than is usually necessary for debugging, but WAY more information than you would get just using rote Python built-ins. It's a bonus. It's not unconventional. I'm not altering what Python gives you. I'm just filling in what you don't get from Python **when you want a stack trace for debug purposes but also want to continue processing**, because I was having trouble debugging without that trace. The only inconvenience I would like to address is the fact that those traces are printed to the console whether the exception is inside a test that expects an exception or not.

Pull request merged by hepcat72: Msruns loader rollback cleanup. ## Summary Change Description This code buffers created `ArchiveFile` records and very cautiously deletes the files in the archive that were created in the event of a rollback. The issue originally was to only exit if the default sequence records could not be found, but I quickly realized that there are all sorts of common exceptions that could happen and leave behind orphaned files: missing sample record (very common), missing sequence detailed in the infile (common), duplicates, missing headers... the list goes on and on. And when I started thinking about having the add a front-loaded loop to handle the infile exceptions for missing sequence records, I started to think of the strategy and eventually creating messy spaghetti code, so I decided a cleaner solution was to simply rollback the directory using a buffer of created ArchiveFile records. I pointed out in the original PR though that there's a potentially better strategy that avoids file deletion: buffer the creation of the files `on_commit` after a `post_save` signal (for each record). I have to think more about this, but in theory, it should work, and be a more comfortable change for those that worry about unintended deletions. however, I for one am very confident in this code. I think that post-save-on-commit would be better, because it's more efficient, but it's the same basic mechanism, which was intended for this express purpose. We should use it IMO. ## Affected Issues/Pull Requests - Resolves #976 ## Review Notes See comments in-line. ## Checklist This pull request will be merged once the following requirements are met. This is now what the user gets from this PR when the maintained field value is incorrect: stalemtf This is what caused the exception to occur: The `last_serum_sample` should be on dev, which is still what it is in my sandbox: ``` In [1]: from DataRepo.models import Animal In [2]: anml = Animal.objects.get(name="20220818M1") In [3]: anml._last_serum_sample() Out[3]: In [4]: anml.last_serum_sample Out[4]: ``` This is what it became on dev: ``` In [1]: from DataRepo.models import Animal In [2]: anml = Animal.objects.get(name="20220818M1") Adding propagation handler to Animal.studies.through In [3]: anml._last_serum_sample() Out[3]: In [4]: anml.last_serum_sample ``` I believe that manual database manipulations caused the value to become `None`. As you can see, the method that generates the value, still generates the correct value. It's just that the value saved got wiped out. Just calling: ``` In [4]: anml.save() ``` automatically fixes the maintained fields: mntfldfixd This PR doesn't fix the values, it just makes it fail gracefully and tell us what needs to be done to fix the problem (in the tooltip). Note, I should have started a screen session yesterday when I ran `rebuild_maintained_fields`, because my session went stale and the rebuild was rolled back. Code pushed by hepcat72: Added an MSRunsLoader class and load_msruns command. This change is not as initially planned and is based on a model change to change the unique constraints of MSRunSample to only allow a single placeholder record for any sample and sequence combo, when there is no mzXML file. When there is an mzXML file, the unique constraint applied is sample, sequence, and mzXML file (via the ms_data_file foreign key into ArchiveFile). The original plan was to make this loading code simpler by decoupling MSRunSample from the connection of PeakGroup to Sample, which would have eliminated the need for placeholder records. See issue #947 for details. Thus this loading code is more complex than originally intended and involves maintaining and updating placeholder records and all the other issues that that causes. The details of the changes (in this and the last 2 commits [in which details had been omitted]) are as follows: - Changes unrelated to the change in the model schema: - Removed from DataRepo/views/upload/validation.py: - get_approx_sample_header_replacement_regex() (replaced with a call to MSRunsLoader.guess_sample_name()) - DEFAULT_SAMPLE_HEADER_SUFFIXES (now lives in MSRunsLoader) - Created a QuerySet class for ArchiveFile that overrides get_or_create to make it usable when providing a file. Django's File() class appends a randomized hash string to file names to avoid collision/overwrites of same-named files, which always results in an attempt to create, followed immediately by a unique constraint violation (since the hash values are the same. So this override excludes the `file_location` value (if provided) from the get_or_create call. It then adds the `file_location` if it was created. - Exception changes - Added an optional "message" argument to the RecordDoesNotExist exception constructor to provide context about how to flesh the Peak Annotation Details sheet for unanalyzed mzXML files - Added exception class: MutuallyExclusiveArgs - Changed the rownum argument to InfileError's constructor so that rows could be referred to by name for the defaults sheet (whose row numbers are not saved) - LoadTable class changes - Made it possible to change the required-ness of options so that I could make --infile optional in the MSRunsLoader and accept just --mzxml-files and either defaults or an infile. - Various typos and documentation fixes - Added MSRunsLoader class/file - I decided to use the defaults defined for the SequencesLoader for Instrument, LC Protocol, Operator, and Date, so that those wouldn't need to be replicated for multiple sheets (Since they are already used with the Sequences sheet, which makes sense, since that is the defining location of those values. This made for a larger init method. - get_create_or_update_msrun_sample_from_row - get_create_or_update_msrun_sample_from_leftover_mzxml - Copied parse_mzxml from the accucor loader (which can be deleted from the accucor loader when it is refactored). - Changes whose complexity increased due to the alternate changes in the model - MSRunSample model changes - Added a custom QuerySet class for the MSRunSample model in order to properly handle placeholder records, because we want to be able to update placeholder records, which are already linked from PeakGroup instead of delete or orphan them, when we would otherwise just want to get_or_create - load_table command changes - Added an "updated" count to the load stats. - TableLoader class changes - Added "updated()" method and associated data to report counts of updated records. - MSRunsLoader class changes - The load_data method is more complex, because it has to account for placeholder records. It means that there can exist rows in the infile that are unassociated with mzXML files, so we have to keep track of mzXML files that had specific sequences assigned in the infile and rows in the infile that have no related mzXML. To try and simplify things, instead of supporting metadata values like polarity that are for placeholder records, I decided to only ever load those values when we have an mzXML file. Then we must traverse the leftover mzXMLs and associate them with default values. Comment on issue by hepcat72: > @hepcat72 Can you help me sort out what additional worksheet, etc. I could create to get these files loaded without having to search/replace underscores with dashes? Or perhaps it would just be simpler to patch the matching code? Interesting. I think fixing the matching code is a good ultimate solution. RN, it uses an exact match of the basename (without the extension) to match (exactly) the header in order to pair the header with the file. If you know the pairs, you can supply either a tsv or excel (with a sheet named "Peak Annotation Details") to supply the mapping between sample, header, and mzXML. When the submission refactor is done, it will be auto-populated (aside from the mzXML), so it's annoying at the moment, but was written to handle resolving any case, and this is a supported case. It has 4 columns (when the header doesn't match the file's base name): sample name, header name, mzxml file name, and annotation file name. A 5th "sequence name" column might currently be necessary*. It's probably best to just show you by example. Download this excel file and look at the "Peak Annotation Details" sheet. That's what you would need. Then you just supply it to `python manage.py msruns_loader --infile ****HERE**** --mzxml-files *.mzXML`. \* I'd like the command line defaults to be more tightly integrated with the "defaults sheet" so that you wouldn't have to enter the sequence name column.

Pull request opened by SjurSutterudSagen: Fix/hover on search in variablebox. When hovering, or focusing the Search in the VariableBox, the outline was only showing in the corners of the Search. This turned out to be two problems, the bottom of the outline was going behind the background of the MixedCheckbox. Which only needed some z-index adjusting to work correctly. The other problem is that the outline goes outside the scrollable list, but with `overflow-y: auto` these are then removed therefore. I could not figure out how to solve this completely, without having to use alot more time. I considered 2 solutions here: 1. To moved the search outside the scrollable list. This should make it look correct, but would remove the scrolling functionality of it. 2. To add an offset on the outline, so it is inside of the scrollable list. I chose to implement option 2 since it was 1 line of code, while keeping the scrolling intact. But this will be discussed with the designer on Monday.

A dict of the keys in `app.app_configs.keys()` returns the following: ``` dict_keys(['admin', 'auth', 'contenttypes', 'sessions', 'messages', 'staticfiles', 'gis', 'postgres', 'django_extensions', 'django_celery_results', 'allauth', 'account', 'socialaccount', 'gitlab', 'django_rename_app', 'core', 'scoring', 'smartflow', 'debug_toolbar']) ``` Each of the AppConfigs in there has a 'name' property that would match the 'rdwatch.scoring' or the 'rdwatch.smartflow'. Pull request merged by mvandenburgh: Restructure application to follow Django/Resonant best practices. Notable changes/improvements: - Global `urls` and `settings` modules are now in the toplevel `rdwatch` app - File structure/other modules are rearranged in accordance with Resonant best practices - The entire app is consolidated into a single Python module, `rdwatch`, with each former app being a submodule of `rdwatch`. Old module structure: ``` rdwatch/ rdwatch_scoring/ rdwatch_smartflow/ ``` New module structure: ``` rdwatch/ core/ scoring/ smartflow/ ``` Notable exceptions missing from this PR: - The default linter/formatter for Resonant is `ruff`; I left our current `flake8`/`black`/`isort` set up alone for now, but we could move to `ruff` in the future. I didn't want to bloat this PR anymore than it already is. - The default python packaging solution for Resonant is `setuptools`. I don't have a strong opinion on this so I left it as `poetry`, we can discuss later if needed but I'm fine with leaving this part alone as it's worked well for us so far.

Pull request merged by mvandenburgh: Allow API key authentication on model run ingest endpoints. This allows the user to authenticate with an API key instead of GitLab oauth on the three endpoints used to create a model run. I've also updated the `scripts/` upload scripts to use this new approach. Currently, the API key is just a global Django setting that we can set; it's really only intended to be used by the SmartFlow upload job. Note, I started out using user-based HTTP Basic Auth, but that didn't work because it would require the user to retrieve a csrf token before making their request. Ideally we don't require a csrf token, but disabling Django's CSRF protection when using basic auth is dangerous because the `Authorization` header used in basic auth is treated the same way as cookies are (i.e., the browser sends it along with any request to the RD-WATCH domain automatically), so it would be vulnerbale to a CSRF attack. Using a non-standard header (`X-RDWATCH-API-KEY` in our case) allows us to safely disable CSRF protection on these three endpoints, as the browser will not send it automatically on every request.

Code pushed by Dabnsky: put os.O_RDWR back into OpenFile() call in TruncateFile() to allow FlushFile()'s f.Sync() call to succeed
Review comment on PR by Dabnsky: The lack of flag means that it is cached. The flag in place means it needs to be downloaded
Review comment on PR by Dabnsky: I could add another value that's simply another downloadRequired bool and check that instead. Does that sound good?

Review comment on PR by Dabnsky: when the file gets flushed, it needs write permissions. I just updated the initial OpenFile() call to also include RDWR flag before it gets downloaded. the flags are now consistent. Does this seem correct to you?

Review comment on PR by jfantinhardesty: Yes, but if it does not have a flag, then it seems like you would not need to continue with the rest of the function since you would know here the file is cached. Also, I am not sure how you use the flag variable here. You set flag := 0 and in the case it is not found, then it is set to 0 and later passed into an OpenFile call, which seems incorrect in the case where the file is already cached.
Review comment on PR by jfantinhardesty: Yeah, that might be a little cleaner to read.
Review comment on PR by jfantinhardesty: Yes, but I don't see why you need an open call on 1378 and then another open call on line 1389.

Review comment on PR by Dabnsky: I was letting it download anyway due to some tests that were now calling DownloadFile() directly instead of OpenFile() as a way to download. the TestHardLimitOnSize was failing because originally, it was returning a nil handle once it failed to find the values in the handle. I could have called OpenFile() before calling DownloadFile() in the test to potentially remedy this. Would that be a more preferable approach? For the flag, what is a better default value to provide? I think I actually need to use the os.O_RD instead of a hard number like I was doing.

Review comment on PR by Dabnsky: the first `OpenFile()` call is for the `DownloadFile()` to take place. This came from Michael's suggestion to call Open instead of creating a new Handle directly like I was doing previously. The second `OpenFile()` call might not be necessary since it was already called previously. That was there previously. The entire else block might not be needed anymore. Do you agree?

Code pushed by Dabnsky: Added isDownloadNeeded value in handle and adjusted download conditionals respectively

Review comment on PR by jfantinhardesty: Yes, I think having the test do OpenFile and then Download is preferable. We shouldn't change out code to make the tests pass. And every time we interact with a file OpenFile is always called first, so that is a reasonable change to this test, and what it was doing before since OpenFile did previously download the file. And I don't think you need a default for the flag here, if you find the flag, then you use that value. If you don't then it didn't need to be downloaded anyway.

Review comment on PR by jfantinhardesty: After looking at this again, I think you can simplify it further. Here I think you are trying to think about it too hard. So you are determining here is the file needs to be downloaded, but there is a ton of logic built into DownloadFile already to figure that out for you. So don't worry about it here. Just call the first OpenFile and then DownloadFile after. It will download it if needed, and it will skip it if not.
Review comment on PR by jfantinhardesty: I think these other checks for Download could be simplified since I believe this logic is already in DownloadFile.

Review comment on PR by jfantinhardesty: I might suggest running this by Michael just to flesh out the design a bit, but my thinking is that you should either have DownloadFile be responsible for checking if a download is required or not (probably prefereable) or the caller of DownloadFile is responsible for checking if a download is required and then it will download it. Right now you are doing a bit of both.

I was able to fully implement this package to work with my Firebase backend, as well as fully customize it to match my theme and localization options. I also implemented pagination which worked beautifully. I did, however, find a few shortcomings where I was not able to find the proper option to customize certain things, which are: - change the default avatar 'if the url was not provided' - set an onError avatar - could be the default 'in case the url was not working, currently just shows a blue circle' - customize the emoji picker - used when clicking the + icon on reactions 'e.g. background color' - customize the user card - found on reactions list 'e.g. add an onTap option to go to user profile/message' - add a padding between the last message and the text field I also have a couple of questions: - when using a custom 'replyPopupBuilder', I can remove the snackbar with 'removeCurrentSnackBar', but how would you remove the emoji reaction popup? - with all the customization options, the file can really grow in size, so is there a recommended way to move all customization variables/functions to a different file, without messing up the controllers/looks etc? Thanks
